items.title: Exact solution of the two-dimensional one-component plasma on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere
items.summary: We solve exactly the two-dimensional one-component plasma at coupling $\Gamma=2$ on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere, a surface of constant negative curvature bounded by two parallels. A conformal map onto a flat cylinder leaves the particles interacting through the flat-cylinder potential, with the curvature entering only through the area element. The partition function becomes a product of incomplete gamma functions, the density is explicit, and all correlations are determinantal. Since the area is bounded, the large-N limit is taken at fixed shape. The free energy, obtained through the constant term with every coefficient in closed form, contains a bulk term (1/2)N ln N, a term linear in N, the flat hard-wall surface tension times the total boundary length, and a shape-dependent constant, with no ln N term. This is the conformal-anomaly prediction for Euler characteristic zero, tested here on a surface where the integrated Gaussian and boundary curvatures are separately nonzero and cancel. The expansion coincides term by term with the cylinder result of Shen and Forrester, whose universal constants are quadratures of the two boundary layers. At both walls the density tends to the flat contact value $n_b$ ln 2, from opposite sides, although the circumferences differ by a factor cosh u_max. We compare the asymptotics with the exact solution up to N=4096, and Monte Carlo simulations at $\Gamma= $1, 4 and 6, validated against the exact $\Gamma= $ 2 density, show how the boundary layers evolve with coupling.

items.title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
authors: Omar Pedraza, Erik D\'iaz-Bautista, L. A. L\'opez, Daniel O-Campa
items.summary: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. Our results show that the $q$-deformation modifies the energy spectra, the behavior of the probability current density components, and the thermodynamic response of the systems. A comparison between monolayer and bilayer graphene reveals distinct thermal behaviors, reflecting their different Landau-level structures and highlighting the influence of the $q$-deformation on their statistical properties.

items.title: Renormalization-Group Foundation of Critical Modes in Correlation Matrices
authors: Yanhua Zhang, Mingmei Xu, Jinghua Fu, Yuanfang Wu
items.summary: Based on the relevant scaling operators of renormalization-group theory, we establish a theoretical framework for constructing complete families of critical-sensitive fluctuation observables and their connected correlation matrices. The corresponding eigenstates of the correlation matrices reveal a hierarchy of multiscale critical correlation patterns and the leading normalized eigenvalues and their ratios show the finite-size scaling behavior. Applying this framework to the two-dimensional Ising model, the correlation matrices associated with both spin and energy operators are constructed. The resulting energy-sector eigenstate patterns, together with the scaling behavior of the leading eigenvalues, provide further support for the proposed framework. Finally, we discuss its potential extension to systems with unknown Hamiltonians.

items.title: The Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic PBC clusters
items.summary: We construct and solve the three-colored Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic lattices with periodic boundary conditions. We describe a self-contained procedure which uses finite quotients of orientation- preserving triangle groups to generate regular maps on compact genus-g surfaces. From these, one can extract their lattice connectivity, plaquette structure, homology cycles and Wilson sectors while implementing consistent boundary conditions. On the example of {8, 3} and {12, 3} lattices, we enumerate a selection of quotients with up to 72 vertices, which constitute the discrete steps in a finite-size scaling analysis. For the isotropic point, corresponding to the spin-liquid phase in the thermodynamic limit, we identify the ground state superselection sectors, quantify their deviation from the homogeneous {\pi} flux sector and show how the selected flux background depends on the quotient geometry. We then discuss how the resulting ground state sector degeneracies are entirely generated by physical lattice symmetries acting on both the plaquette fluxes and non-contractible Wilson loops. Finally, we study the behaviour of the finite-size two-vison gap and matter fermion correlations. We find that the gap does not decrease monotonically with increasing system size, while one still recovers the expected algebraic decay of the correlations at the isotropic point, even for the considered modest system sizes.

items.title: Probing Phase Fluctuations in Cuprates by Multidimensional Josephson Spectroscopy
authors: Albert Liu, Danica Pavicevic, Alex G\'omez Salvador, Marios H. Michael, Michael Fechner, Pedro M. Lozano, Qiang Li, Genda D. Gu, Eugene Demler, Andrea Cavalleri
items.summary: The normal state of cuprate superconductors is believed to host precursor electron pairing above the superconducting transition temperature. These pre-formed pairs, which extend over an unknown temperature range, are expected to lack long-range phase coherence. Because spectroscopic evidence for this hypothesis is only indirect, new methods to probe these physics are needed. Nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy allows one to probe high-order time correlation functions and is therefore sensitive to fluctuations. Measurements of third-harmonic generation along the superconducting planes have revealed responses persisting above Tc, but a clear relation between these optical responses and specific properties of the fluctuating state has not yet been established. Here, we apply angle-resolved multidimensional terahertz spectroscopy to probe the optical nonlinearity of the Josephson tunneling resonance in La1.83Sr0.17CuO4 across the superconducting to normal state transition. We find that among all third-order nonlinear responses, the non-rephasing multidimensional signal is especially sensitive to non-mean field fluctuations of the order parameter. We measure a crossover occurring at T ~ Tc between a mean-field optical nonlinearity that dominates at low temperatures and one that is mediated by short-range superconducting fluctuations. We present a theoretical framework that connects the out-of-plane optical response in both regimes to the fluctuating in-plane superconducting state, and contrast the sensitivity of different types of terahertz nonlinearities to fluctuating order.

items.title: Quantitative Theory for the Amplitude of Fluorescence Quantum Beats from Geminate Triplet-Pair Fusion
authors: Zachary Rex, B\'ach Pham Xu\^an, Gerald Curran III, Ivan Biaggio
items.summary: We derive the amplitude of fluorescence quantum beats caused by geminate triplet-exciton fusion from the full set of parameters that characterize singlet fission and triplet exciton dynamics. We apply the theory to tetracene and rubrene single crystals. We find that the amplitude depends on the fission time in tetracene, but does not do so in rubrene, where it is determined by the dimensionality of triplet transport. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the experimental data in both materials, for a fission time of the order of 200 ps and isotropic triplet transport in tetracene, and for a triplet hopping time along the herringbone axis of 200-300 ps and anisotropic transport in rubrene.

items.title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
items.summary: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero

items.title: On the richness of metamaterials generated by recursive cell division
items.summary: Scale-rich metamaterials are one member of a family of recursive cell divisions, which differ in which cell is cut, where the cut passes and at what angle. We characterise six members of this family through three network mappings, the cell tree, the dual graph of ligaments and junctions, and the frame graph of spans, and through their elastic-wave properties: the effective refractive index n, its isotropy and the band over which it holds. The dual-graph degree law, the mean degree and the age law of the ligaments hit by new ones are the same for every rule, so they cannot distinguish the materials. The cell tree and the cell shapes do differ, and one consequence of them explains the physics: the tail of long spans in the frame graph. With the longest spans as the length scale, the bending part of the inverse squared index follows a single power law across rules, densities and numbers of ligaments, and the same spans set the lowest local resonance and the band edge. The stretching part, which caps the index, is carried by the straight frame lines of the tiling rather than by the division. Random cut angles produce elongated cells and long spans, hence high index and a narrow band; cuts perpendicular to the long axis of the cell keep the cells compact, giving low index and a wide band. Cutting through the centroid instead of a random point bounds the split fraction between 4/9 and 5/9, which removes the area hierarchy without changing the index. The cut angle interpolates continuously between these limits, and the isotropy peaks where the ligament orientations become isotropic while the cells are still compact. In three dimensions the plate and strut divisions are stretching dominated and the index stays low for every rule.

items.title: Remark on internal relaxation in large number qubit systems
items.summary: For a time $t_{c}$ of calculation in an $N$ qubit quantum computer that is much shorter than the intrinsic Heisenberg time $t_H$, $t_c\ll t_H$, the dynamics of the system is effectively irreversible and the couplings between the qubits give rise to a relaxation time scale $\tau_r$. If $t_H\gg t_c >\sim \tau_r$ one looses quantum coherence exponentially fast. Since $t_H$ scales exponentially with $N$ there is a threshold $N_c$ such that for $N\gg N_c$ one must be aware of possible intrinsic relaxation during calculation. As an order of magnitude estimation we find $N_c\approx \ln(\tau_r/T)$ where $T$ is a typical system specific oscillation time of a single qubit. $\tau_r$ can be estimated as the typical inverse transition rate between two parts of the system, one of which is treated as an environment of the other.

items.title: Phonon-mediated intrinsic topological superconductivity in Fermi arcs
authors: Kristian M{\ae}land, Masoud Bahari, Bj\"orn Trauzettel
items.summary: We propose that phonons can intrinsically mediate topological superconductivity on the surface of Weyl semimetals. Weyl semimetals are gapless topological materials with nondegenerate zero energy surface states known as Fermi arcs. We derive the phonon spectrum and electron-phonon coupling in an effective model of a Weyl semimetal and apply weak-coupling Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer theory of superconductivity. In a slab geometry, we find that surface superconductivity dominates over bulk superconductivity in a range of chemical potentials around the Weyl nodes. The superconducting gap function realizes spinless chiral $p$-wave Cooper pairing in the Fermi arcs, leading to Majorana bound states in the core of vortices. Furthermore, we find a suppression of the absolute value of the gap in the center of the Fermi arcs, which is not captured by a local Hubbard attraction. The suppression is due to the nonlocal origin of electron-phonon coupling, leading to a layer dependence which has important consequences for topological surface states.

items.title: Optically Induced Thermal Runaway in Phase-Change VO 2 Nanostructures
authors: Jiří Kabát, Peter Kepič, Andrea Konečná, and Filip Ligmajer
items.summary: Abstract While thermal runaway occurs across diverse physical disciplines, its presence in subwavelength phase-change photonics remains unexplored because existing thermo-optic models break down near sharp optical transitions. Here, we introduce an iterative multiphysics framework coupling full-wave electrodynamics with heat transfer, and we report on optically induced thermal runaway in vanadium dioxide (VO 2 ) nanostructures. The runaway switching threshold depends on the illumination wavelength, ambient temperature, and underlying substrate, with external thermal biasing significantly reducing the optical intensity required for runaway ignition. Our results provide insights into sharp thermo-optic transitions and essential design principles for active metasurfaces, neuromorphic photonic devices, and nanoscale thermal management based on phase-change materials.

items.title: Light Switchable Plasmon–Exciton Coupling at the Nanoscale via Photoresponsive Azobenzene Ligands
authors: Tal Binyamin, Sergei Remennik, and Lioz Etgar
items.summary: Abstract Precise control of plasmon–exciton interactions is essential for optoelectronic and light-harvesting applications. Here, photoreversible azobenzene ligands enable light-controlled assembly of gold (Au) and CsPbBr 3 perovskite nanoparticles (NPs), with matched surface plasmon resonance and bandgap energies. Under 365 nm UV illumination, trans -to- cis isomerization reduces ligand solubility, bringing NPs into the proximity of each other and enhancing perovskite photoluminescence (PL) and radiative recombination rates. Electron energy loss spectroscopy reveals plasmon–exciton coupling through changes in perovskite bulk plasmon excitations and Au plasmon resonance. Halide tuning further demonstrates that maximizing spectral overlap, achieved at 70% Br, optimizes PL enhancement. Subsequent 450 nm illumination reverses ligand isomerization, redispersing the NPs and switching off the enhancement. This reversible, light-responsive hybrid nanostructure provides a versatile platform for externally controlled nanoscale optoelectronic applications.

items.title: Direct Measurement of the Quantum Capacitance in Oxide Semiconductors Using an Electric-Field-Penetration Technique
authors: Kisoo Nam, Chang Niu, Aravindh Shankar, Jian-Yu Lin, Sanjeev Khare, Sumi Lee, Pramey Upadhyaya, and Peide D. Ye
items.summary: Abstract Indium-based oxide semiconductor (OS) field-effect transistors (FETs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation monolithic three-dimensional (3D) integration, but a limited understanding of channel capacitance hinders further scaling. Here, we measure quantum capacitance ( C q ) in In-based OS channels by using a lock-in-based electric-field-penetration technique (eFPT). A small AC voltage modulation superimposed on the back-gate DC bias induces an electric field at the top gate, detected as an AC current ( I TG ). Normalizing this current to its full depletion reference ( I TG 0 ) enables C q extraction. Linear current scaling with frequency, excitation amplitude, and device area, together with an invariant normalized response, supports robust capacitance extraction. In the accumulation regime, an increase in C q with DC bias is observed, which is consistent with band nonparabolicity and occupation of higher energy subbands. Finally, thicker InO x channels and higher In concentrations in InGaZnO (IGZO) films exhibit a larger C q . These findings demonstrate the feasibility of tailoring C q in In-based OS FETs.

items.title: Spatial Phonon Coherence Limits Wave-Like Heat Transport in Nanostructures
authors: Zhongwei Zhang, Honglei Wang, Zhiwei Guo, Sebastian Volz, and Jie Chen
items.summary: Abstract The wave nature of lattice vibrations is central to phonon dynamics, heat transport, and coupling to other excitations, yet its effective spatial range in realistic nanostructures remains unclear. We identify spatial phonon coherence length as an intrinsic scale that defines the extent of thermal phonon wavepackets and limits wave-like heat transport. Across resonant systems and superlattices, thermal phonons exhibit short coherence lengths over a broad terahertz frequency range. This finite coherence limits resonance-induced phonon hybridization and thermal conductivity suppression, while also governing the coherent–incoherent crossover, band folding, Bragg scattering, and minimum thermal conductivity in superlattices. A coherence-based lattice-dynamics framework further captures the spatially limited nature of these wave phenomena. Our results establish spatial phonon coherence length as a common descriptor connecting localized resonance and propagating coherent transport, providing a nanoscale criterion for controlling heat conduction through structural design.

items.title: Capacitance-Engineered Threshold Switching Transistors with 4 mV/dec Subthreshold Swing
authors: Fansheng Peng, Zhiyi Cui, Yanhong Zhou, Dehuan Meng, Lian-Mao Peng, and Chenguang Qiu
items.summary: Abstract The subthreshold swing (SS) of conventional field-effect transistors (FETs) is fundamentally constrained by the thermionic emission governed by the Boltzmann distribution, imposing a theoretical minimum of 60 mV/dec at room temperature. Here, we report an aligned carbon nanotube transistor (A-CNT FET) that achieves an exceptionally steep SS. By integrating an HfO 2 -based threshold-switching (TS) device in series with the gate of the A-CNT FET, we realize steep-slope switching behavior. The fabricated device exhibits an SS as low as 4 mV/dec and an on/off ratio of 3 × 10 5 . Notably, the short-channel device ( L ch = 50 nm) delivers an on-state current of 1 mA/μm while maintaining an SS of 12 mV/dec. Furthermore, scaling the capacitance of the TS device optimizes the voltage division between the TS device and the transistor, yielding synergistic improvements in both the on/off ratio and SS. This work establishes an effective strategy for high-performance steep-switching carbon nanotube transistors.

items.title: Enhancing soil carbon to address the joint climate and biodiversity crises
High-rate and durable sodium-ion batteries enabled by charge-asymmetric single-atom-energized hard carbon
items.summary: Abstract Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) represent a promising complement to lithium-based systems due to the abundant supply and cost-effectiveness of sodium. However, the widespread adoption of SIBs is practically hindered by the lack of cycling-stable hard-carbon anodes with superior capacity and rate capability. Here, we show a design of high-rate and durable SIB anodes achieved by introducing main-group metal single atoms ( M SA = Sb, Bi, Sn) featuring a unique charge-asymmetric N 4 – M SA –O 2 moiety anchored on nitrogen-doped hard carbon ( M SA @NC). This designed charge-asymmetric configuration establishes a dynamically evolving atomic interface that adaptively modulates active sites to achieve significant improvements in both Na + storage kinetics and capacity. The representative Sb SA @NC system demonstrates high specific capacity, improved rate capability and cyclability in both coin and pouch-type cells. Extensive experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the structural rearrangement of the N 4 –Sb–O 2 moiety during (de)sodiation is highly reversible and energetically favorable, enabling enhanced reversible capacity (422.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 ) and rate capability (207.6 mAh g −1 at 20 A g −1 ) while preserving material integrity. This work offers a promising pathway in advancing high-performing HC anodes for fast-charging and durable SIBs.

items.title: Single-atom catalyst–Li2O2 interfacial chemistry governs the activity–stability trade-off in Li–O2 batteries
items.summary: Abstract Cathode catalysts in aprotic Li–O 2 batteries are commonly judged by their ability to lower charge overpotentials, yet improved catalytic activity often does not lead to durable cycling. Here, we use structurally well-defined M–N 4 single-atom catalysts (SACs) as model cathodes to elucidate the interplay between catalyst activity and battery stability. Integrated experimental and theoretical studies suggest that, although SACs promote Li 2 O 2 oxidation and lower the initial charging overpotential, they also increase the reactivity of discharge-generated Li 2 O 2 toward ether electrolytes, promoting carboxylate accumulation and cathode passivation. On the basis of this mechanistic insight, a localized high-concentration electrolyte is introduced to regulate the catalyst–Li 2 O 2 interfacial chemistry, suppress side reactions, and extend the cycling life from 42 to 398 cycles. This work identifies a previously overlooked trade-off between catalytic activity and battery stability in Li–O 2 batteries and provides a mechanistic foundation for designing stable catalyst/electrolyte interfaces in high-energy electrochemical devices.

items.title: Non-Hermitian skin effect and quasiperiodicity-induced localization in a photonic lattice with staggered on-site potentials
authors: Jia-Yi Li, Zhi-Xu Zhang, Jie Zhang, Kai-Xin Hu, Wen-Xue Cui, Ji Cao and Hong-Fu Wang
items.summary: The quasicrystals combined with nonreciprocal and on-site non-Hermiticity provide a unique platform to explore exceptional phenomena arising from the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). Especially, we investigate a non-Hermitian photonic lattice with nonreciprocal hoppings and staggered complex on-site potentials, revealing an energy-dependent bipolar NHSE and a quasiperiodicity-driven redistribution from skin states to bulk-localized states. Numerical winding numbers and analytical contact conditions reveal the spectral reconnections underlying the bipolar NHSE, with the sign of the imaginary eigenenergy determining its localization direction. Meanwhile, imaginary quasiperiodic modulation drives a crossover from skin localization to bulk localization, while real and imaginary modulations yield comparable bulk localization at strong modulation. Moreover, Fibonacci-size calculations support persistent skin–bulk coexistence, while a separable two-dimensional extension connects one-dimensional localization directions to corner accumulation and spatial redistribution. These results provide a unified framework for understanding and controlling the interplay between spectral topology and quasiperiodicity in non-Hermitian photonic systems.

items.title: Gadolinium-Integrated Ce6 Hybrid Nanoparticles for Enhanced Ultrasound-Activated Afterglow Luminescence and MR Imaging
authors: Jiahui Sun, Yukun Wang, Zhe Li, Xingyue Fan, Qingpeng Zhang, Baoli Yin, Hengxin Shen, Ying Zhang, Peng Liang, Jiaqi Fu, Rui Yin, Yuzhen Yu, Ying Zhou, Cheng Zhang, Wenming He, and Guosheng Song
items.summary: Abstract Fluorescence imaging is sensitive but limited by autofluorescence and poor light penetration. Afterglow imaging reduces background, yet light-activated probes are hard to activate in deep tissues. Ultrasound-activated afterglow uses penetrant ultrasound, but current probes exhibit weak luminescence and lack anatomical reference. We develop Ce6-Gd NPs for dual-modal ultrasound-afterglow and T 1 -MRI. Ce6 NPs show 23-fold stronger afterglow than bilirubin (BL) NPs, and Gd 3+ incorporation further amplifies it by 3-fold, associated with enhanced ROS generation, offering a new strategy to boost ultrasound-induced luminescence. Gd 3+ also provides T 1 relaxivity 19-fold higher than Gd-DOTA, serving as an efficient MRI contrast agent. Ce6-Gd NPs generate detectable afterglow through 2.5 cm chicken breast and allow repeatable activation. In vivo, local injection enables tumor imaging and MRI contrast, while intravenous injection visualizes abdominal tumors in an orthotopic pancreatic model.

items.title: Emergent Attraction and Competing Orders near the Van Hove Singularity in Rhombohedral $n$-layer Graphene
items.summary: Unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral $n$-layer graphene exhibits a rich phase diagram with multiple distinct superconducting regions, whose microscopic origins remain unclear. Here, we investigate the competition between charge-density-wave (CDW) and pair-density-wave (PDW) instabilities near the inner van Hove singularities (VHSs), using a patch renormalization-group approach with the realistic band structures incorporated. We identify two key findings. First, we find an effective attractive interaction emerging from purely repulsive interactions through RG flow in the presence of $C_3$ symmetry breaking. The resulting interaction structure, with two repulsive couplings and one attractive coupling, gives rise to competing CDW and PDW instabilities. Second, the competition is controlled by the detuning from the VHS. While CDW dominates near the VHS filling and at higher temperatures, PDW becomes the leading instability on either side of the VHS and at lower temperatures. This mechanism naturally produces two superconducting regions separated by a CDW-dominated regime, providing a possible qualitative explanation for the experimentally observed separation between SC1 and SC2.

items.title: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
items.summary: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension. While in one dimension an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy guarantees an exact matrix product state representation with a bond dimension independent of the system size, an analogous statement does not hold for general states in two dimensions (2D). This leaves open the question of how the expressivity of 2D TNS is related to the entanglement properties of the states they represent. In this work, we focus on two families of 2D translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states: single-band BCS superconductors and half-filled two-band insulators (including semimetals). For each family, we prove that an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy is equivalent to having an exact Gaussian fermionic TNS representation with a finite bond dimension determined by the Renyi-0 entropy. We also establish equivalent characterizations in terms of compactly supported Wannier-type orbitals and the momentum-space wavefunction, relating the spatial extent of these orbitals and the structure of the wavefunction to the required bond dimension.

items.title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states
items.summary: Under unitary dynamics preserving a global symmetry, bipartite entanglement typically grows while an initially broken symmetry is locally restored. Here, we show that this conventional scenario can be reversed when symmetry-breaking coherence is initially encoded in long-range entanglement. We investigate this phenomenon in a family of charge deformed crosscap states, characterized by antipodal entangled pairs with tunable entanglement and symmetry breaking. We first characterize their static properties, finding a Page-like entanglement profile and an entanglement asymmetry that vanishes for subsystems smaller than half the system size, but grows logarithmically for larger subsystems. For symmetric subsystems, we also analyze the symmetry-resolved entanglement and investigate how it evolves as the subsystem is continuously deformed away from a symmetric partition. Following a quench to a free-fermion tight-binding chain, we uncover an unconventional dynamics in which the entanglement entropy decreases whereas the entanglement asymmetry increases, so that initially symmetric subsystems dynamically develop local symmetry breaking. This behavior is quantitatively captured by a quasiparticle picture describing the propagation of antipodal correlations. Our results reveal how symmetry-preserving dynamics can redistribute globally encoded symmetry-breaking coherence, making it locally accessible, and establish the initial entanglement structure as a key ingredient in determining the fate of local symmetries out of equilibrium.

items.title: Local interference algorithms for observables in large random circuits
items.summary: In quantum dynamics, it is generally believed that interference effects lead to a sign problem for classical Monte Carlo sampling methods, rendering sampling ineffective. In this paper we show that this is generically not the case for the task of simulating the evolution of observables in random instances of circuit dynamics. Specifically, we consider two examples of observables which give large signals despite the randomness of the dynamics: first order out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in unstructured random circuits without conservation laws and time-ordered charge-charge correlators (TOCs) in particle number-preserving random circuits. We show that these observables can be approximated by classical stochastic processes and that these approximations can be systematically improved with a series expansion that incorporates coherent corrections associated with clusters of gates. We design and implement algorithms that combine Monte Carlo sampling and tensor network methods to approximate the series. We observe numerically that the computational complexity of approximating TOCs and OTOCs scales polynomially in the circuit size and in the target precision. We study the accuracy of these algorithms by directly mapping their ensemble-averaged errors to partition functions of replica statistical models, allowing for perturbative analysis and numerics in $1$d brickwork geometries. Our theoretical analysis explains the empirical observation of polynomial complexity of these algorithms and is consistent with polynomial complexity extending to arbitrarily small precision and to the thermodynamic limit.

items.title: Effect of superplastic deformation on the intergranular corrosion resistance of austenitic steel 321 with different types of UFG structure: A case of homogeneous and heterogeneous microstructure obtained by ECAP
items.summary: The effects of superplasticity (SP) on the structure, hardness, and intergranular corrosion (IGC) resistance of UFG 321L steel are reported. By increasing the number of the ECAP cycles (N) and varying the ECAP temperature, and annealing temperature, the degree of the microstructural heterogeneity was changed. Regardless of the microstructural homogeneity degree, UFG steels demonstrated the possibility of realizing the SP effect at temperatures below the onset temperature of dynamic recrystallization. The dependence of ductility of the UFG steel on the test temperature is non-monotonic with a minimum at 450-600C. The maximum elongation to failure (~250%) was achieved at a SP temperature of 800C. The SP deformation of the UFG steel is controlled by the power law creep. It is shown that the hardness of UFG steel samples after SP is equal than the hardness of UFG steels annealed at the same temperature. It is also shown what SP leads to a decrease in the IGC resistance of the UFG steel. Heterostructured steel have reduced ductility, as well as lower resistance to IGC after tension tests at room temperature (RT). The minimum IGC resistance is ensured at N=2, and the maximum - at N=4. The IGC resistance of homogeneous UFG samples after tension testing exceeds the IGC resistance of coarse-grained steel. Tension test at a RT has the greatest negative effect on the IGC resistance of heterostructured steel, and the least negative effect on the IGC resistance of homogeneous steel. Increasing the number of ECAP cycles enhances the ductility of the UFG steel at 750-900C. Increasing the ECAP temperature results in a simultaneous decrease in ductility and flow stress. Heterostructured steel exhibits minimal values of the activation energy of SP deformation. Increasing the number of ECAP cycles and increasing the ECAP temperature lead to an increase in the activation energy of SP deformation.

items.title: Multiple Field-Induced Transitions, Magnetocaloric Response and Anisotropic Magnetotransport in Orthorhombic RAlGe (R = Dy, Ho)
items.summary: We present a comprehensive study of the magnetic, thermodynamic, and magnetocaloric properties of single-crystalline DyAlGe and HoAlGe, both members of the RAlGe Weyl semimetal family. Magnetization, heat capacity and transport measurements reveal multiple magnetic phase transitions associated with the evolution of complex magnetic structures. For DyAlGe, the primary magnetic ordering occurs at \textit{$T_{N1}$}= 30.5 K , while HoAlGe orders at a much lower temperature of \textit{$T_{N1}$}= 11.5 K, followed by additional first-order magnetic transitions at 6.6 K and 8 K, respectively. The magnetization isotherms display pronounced anisotropy for the B $\parallel$ a, consistent with competing exchange and crystal-field interactions. The magnetic entropy change ($ΔS_M$) derived from isothermal magnetization demonstrates a significant magnetocaloric effect (MCE) with sign change in both systems, with a maximum $ΔS_M$ of $\approx$ 5$-$23 J/kg-K along B $\parallel$ a for a field change of 0$-$7 T. The sign reversal of $ΔS_M$ across field-induced transitions highlights the complex field-tuned spin configurations. The moderate MCE and magnetic anisotropy suggest that these materials may serve as model systems for studying magnetocaloric effects in topologically nontrivial intermetallics with interplay between localized 4\textit{f} magnetism and crystal symmetry.

items.title: Photon condensation driven by scalar spin chirality
items.summary: Gauge invariance forbids equilibrium photon condensation for spatially uniform electric-dipole coupling, motivating alternative routes based on orbital magnetic response. We show that triangular molecular magnets coupled to a cavity support photon condensation driven by emergent scalar spin chirality. Starting from the half-filled Hubbard model in the Mott regime, we derive an effective Hamiltonian in which virtual ring exchange couples the cavity flux directly to scalar spin chirality. Mean-field theory, collective-fluctuation calculations, and finite-size exact diagonalization reveal a phase with spontaneous chirality ordering and a macroscopic cavity displacement, together with hybrid chirality-photon excitations. The condensation threshold can be tuned electrically through the molecular chirality splitting. Our results establish emergent orbital degrees of freedom in frustrated magnets as a route to equilibrium light-matter ordering beyond conventional dipolar cavity quantum electrodynamics.

items.title: Richtmyer-Meshkov instability induced by a Gaussian-kicked rotor-like potential in a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate
items.summary: This research investigates the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability within a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate. We offer a kicking potential that replicates the impulsive shock across both interfaces of the three-component BEC to trigger the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability. We propose a hydrodynamic model that indicates the essential criteria for the onset of hydrodynamic instability in the BEC through the application of the hydrodynamic pressure equation. We utilise the split-step Crank-Nicolson method to numerically solve the coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations, with the objective of obtaining the immiscible ground state of all components in a quasi-2D harmonic trap. Following this, we introduce a Gaussian-like disruption instigated by the kick rotor model at both interfaces of the confined three-component BEC to explore the time-dependent development of nonlinear hydrodynamic instability patterns, culminating in quantum turbulence and nonlinear configurations at the interfaces. The kinetic energy spectra of both the incompressible and compressible elements of the system exhibit scaling in the low-wavenumber domain with power-law exponents of $-5/3$ and $1$, respectively. Conversely, the high-wavenumber domain is defined by $k^{-4}$ and $k^{-7/2}$ scaling for the incompressible and compressible elements, respectively, aligning with the established spectral characteristics of quantum turbulence. This research offers fresh perspectives on the mechanisms of hydrodynamic instability, vortex generation, non-equilibrium pattern evolution, and quantum turbulence in superfluid systems comprising multiple interacting elements.

items.title: Competing Magnetic Orders and Continuously Varying Exponents in $U(1)$ Spin Liquids
items.summary: Unequal couplings to a common emergent gauge field provide a continuous way to tune competing magnetic instabilities in an effective description of $U(1)$ spin-liquid mixtures. We study this mechanism in quantum electrodynamics in 2+1 dimensions with two families of four-component Dirac fermions. Combining a leading large-$N$ treatment with Schwinger--Dyson equations, we obtain chiral condensates representing Néel order in the two sectors. At fixed fermion number, the coupling ratio $κ=e_2^2/e_1^2$ controls which condensates develop. Depending on $N$, the phases with a single condensate are connected through either coexistence or a finite interval in which both fermion families remain gapless. The mass-generation thresholds are reciprocal, and the fermion gaps close with Miransky essential singularities. The renormalization group flow has a circular line of fixed points parametrized by the invariant ratio $κ$. At the calculated order, gauge-invariant staggered magnetization correlations have continuously varying exponents in the gapless regime, while the exponent for correlations between the two sectors is independent of $κ$. These results connect the competition between magnetic orders to a continuous family of critical theories and identify magnetic correlation signatures of the intervening gapless regime.

items.title: An Effective Theory for Hot Lines
items.summary: We develop a high-temperature effective theory for spatial conformal line defects in theories with thermal screening. The defect partition function admits a local geometric expansion, whose leading terms describe the effective tension and bending response of the line. Using a convergent bulk OPE for heavy-state defect matrix elements, we derive asymptotic relations for averaged products of defect one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime $1 \ll Δ_χ\ll Δ^{1/d}$. We compute the leading EFT coefficients for a twisted free scalar and for the magnetic line at the $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point, large-$N$ Gross--Neveu model and $\mathcal N = 2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory. For the three-dimensional Ising model, Monte Carlo simulations yield a perimeter coefficient in good agreement with a Padé interpolation of our $\varepsilon$-expansion result.

items.title: Dynamics of a Single-Domain Dissipative Magnetic Gyroscope in Electric and Magnetic Fields
items.summary: We formulate the coupled spin--rotation dynamics of a single-domain symmetric top ferromagnetic needle (a magnetic gyroscope) in static magnetic and electric fields. The conservative Hamiltonian contains the rotational kinetic energy, the magnetocrystalline and shape anisotropy, the Zeeman energy, the electrostatic energy of the dipole induced in the conducting needle, the linear magnetoelectric coupling, and the relativistic motional (spin-orbit) coupling. Gilbert damping is introduced, and in an electric field, Debye relaxation of the induced electric dipole of the conducting needle also results in dissipation. We give the equations of motion in the laboratory and body-fixed frames, with singularity-free quaternion kinematics. For a 120-nm-long single-domain cobalt needle in a 0.5~T field we find: (i) because the anisotropy field ($\approx 1.3$~T) exceeds the applied magnetic field, the spin reverses direction several times during the initial Gilbert-damping transient, and the parity of the number of reversals determines whether the easy axis ends up parallel or antiparallel to the spin; (ii) after the transient the needle librates about the field---precession accompanied by nutation at twice the precession frequency---with a period of about 20~ns, consistent with the libration period $2π(I_1/μB)^{1/2}$, while the Zeeman and rotational kinetic energies oscillate out of phase and the total energy is conserved; (iii) a static electric field $\mathbf E$ exerts on the conducting needle a shape-dependent polarization torque that tends to align the long axis of the needle with $\mathbf E$. The torques due to the magnetoelectric interaction and motional magnetic fields ($\lesssim1~μ$T) are negligible compared with the polarization torque. A conducting needle can therefore serve as a magnetometer only if $E\ll E_c$.

items.title: Localized corrosion resistance of ultrafine-grained austenitic steel 321 obtained by Rotary Swaging: The role of annealing conditions
items.summary: The object of this study was austenitic steel 321, which has an ultrafine-grained (UFG) structure formed by Rotary Swaging (RS). RS leads to the formation of a two-phase macroscopically heterogeneous and, at the same time, a microscopically homogeneous UFG structure with an increased content of martensite. It has been shown that secondary TiC nanoparticles form in the annealing at 450-550C, the reverse transformation of martensite into austenite occurs at 550-650C, and recrystallization begins at 700C. Electrochemical studies of the resistance of the UFG steel to general corrosion, intergranular corrosion (IGC), and pitting corrosion (PC) have been carried out. It has been shown that the UFG steel after RS has a reduced IGC resistance. The surface of steel rods after RS has a reduced hardness and corrosion resistance compared to the central part of the rods. It has been shown that in the temperature range of 450-550C, there is a slight increase in the microhardness, and a significant decrease in the IGC and PC resistance of the UFG steel. Recrystallization at 700-800C leads to an increased PC resistance and IGC resistance. Annealing conditions have been determined that ensure a good combination of strength, ductility and corrosion resistance of the UFG steel. It was demonstrated that to explain the non-monotonic variation in the localized corrosion rate of UFG steel during annealing, it is necessary to consider not only the well-known effects of martensite and delta-ferrite, but also the precipitation of TiC particles and the changes in the free energy of non-equilibrium grain boundaries.

items.title: Interface-Selective Extreme Ultraviolet Second Harmonic Generation Away from Linear Absorption Edges
items.summary: Extreme ultraviolet (XUV) second harmonic generation (SHG) combines interface selectivity with core-level element specificity but has so far been limited to linear absorption edges. Here, we measure XUVSHG from an indium tin oxide capped MoO$_3$/SiO$_2$/Si photovoltaic heterojunction for fundamental energies of 60--76\,eV, below the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge. Where linear absorption is a featureless valence background, we observe a strong, structured XUVSHG response with maxima near 70 and 76\,eV. Layer-resolved first-principles calculations reproduce both maxima and assign them to the Si/SiO$_2$ interface, the 76\,eV peak to the bridging Si monolayer and the 70\,eV peak to the near-interface substrate. Bethe--Salpeter calculations for bulk Si connect the signal to Si 2$p$ excitons at 140--160\,eV. At the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge, the calculated response is instead governed by MoO$_3$-induced asymmetry at the oxide interface. These findings establish off-edge XUV SHG as a powerful approach for selectively probing distinct buried interfaces within complex material heterostructures.

items.title: Color Through Time: Distributions, Sparsity and Dominance in Western Painting
items.summary: We investigate the evolution of color in Western painting using a large corpus of digitized artworks. Each painting is represented by its distribution over a fixed palette of colors in a perceptually uniform space. We compare the color distributions of historical periods and artistic movements through their Jensen-Shannon distances, and introduce two interpretable descriptors, sparsity and dominance, that quantify how many colors are used and how unevenly they are represented. We find a historical transition from dark, earthy palettes toward a broader and more saturated chromatic range, unfolding through distinct shifts from the nineteenth century onward. Periods evolve smoothly over time, whereas artistic movements display increasingly distinct chromatic signatures beyond chronology. In the sparsity-dominance plane, painting follows a two-stage historical trajectory, first broadening the range of colors used and later increasing color dominance. Comparison with natural images reveals distinct ways in which artistic palettes depart from nature, either through the colors they use or through how broadly and evenly those colors are distributed. Finally, two surveys on generated images show that judgments of harmonious color balance concentrate around two complementary regimes: many colors arranged in a strong hierarchy, or few colors used evenly.

items.title: Non-equilibrium topological order from Floquet anyon proliferation in the toric code
items.summary: We analyze the dynamics of Kitaev's toric code in Floquet quenches where the drive coherently creates and propagates fermionic $f$ anyons. We show that the long-time state departs from pure-state topological order but retains long-range entanglement, thereby realizing a Floquet analog of intrinsic mixed-state topological order. As a key result enabling this analysis, we derive decompositions of the entanglement entropy and logarithmic negativity that separate the ground-state value, including topological terms, from a contribution given by the driven quasiparticles. For a drive inducing non-interacting $f$ dynamics, these decompositions allow us to leverage numerical methods for free fermions and to link the emergence of the proposed long-time ordered state to the equilibration of $f$ anyons to a periodic Gibbs ensemble. For drives inducing Floquet eigenstate thermalization of $f$, our results suggest a scenario where Floquet heating of the $f$ sector stabilizes a genuine non-equilibrium topological phase, in contrast with the usual view of heating as an obstacle to order in periodically driven systems.

items.title: Charge-transfer excitation drives cooperative phonon-assisted exciton self-trapping in NiPS$_3$
items.summary: Carrier self-trapping is a fundamental relaxation pathway in strongly correlated quantum materials, yet the microscopic lattice motions that drive it have remained largely inaccessible to direct observation. Here we investigate the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS$_3$ upon excitation across its ligand-to-metal charge-transfer gap, and reveal a nonequilibrium pathway that initially generates unbound carriers before they evolve into correlated excitonic states. Using ultrabroadband optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy, we simultaneously track carrier localization and the associated lattice dynamics in real time. The transient conductive response quenches with a time constant of $\sim$109 fs and evolves into a localized exciton state, accompanied by pronounced renormalization of Ni-S optical phonons and the emergence of a transient 2.7 THz vibrational mode. Temperature-dependent measurements, together with mode-resolved dielectric dynamics and symmetry analysis, identify the 2.7 and 8.0 THz responses as spectroscopic indicators of exciton self-trapping and point to a cooperative two-phonon mechanism. These findings establish the excitation pathway as a key parameter controlling carrier localization and many-body relaxation in strongly coupled quantum materials.

items.title: Specific heat in the BCS-rashbon BEC crossover regime of an ultracold Fermi gas with a 3D spherical spin-orbit coupling
items.summary: We theoretically investigate strong-coupling properties of an ultracold Fermi gas with a tunable spherical (isotropic) spin-orbit interaction. In this spin-orbit coupled system, it is known that a two-body bound state, called rashbon, can be formed even in the coupling regime where a pairing interaction alone cannot form such a two-body bound molecule. In this paper, we evaluate the specific heat at constant volume $C_V$, including pairing fluctuations in the presence of SOC within the framework of the strong-coupling theory developed by Nozières and Schmitt-Rink, to show that this thermodynamic quantity is very useful to see how system properties vary from a Fermi gas to a rashbon gas with increasing spin-orbit coupling strength. At the superfluid phase transition temperature $T_{\rm c}$, $C_V$ is found to exhibit a peak structure in the intermediate spin-orbit coupling regime between the weak-coupling Fermi gas regime and a strong-SOC rashbon gas regime. In the normal state above $T_{\rm c}$, from detailed analyses of the temperature dependences of $C_V$, we also identify the regions where system properties are dominated by (1) a Fermi atomic gas, (2) a Bose gas of stable rashbons, and (3) fluctuating rashbons. Combining these results with the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS)--Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) crossover physics realized by tuning the strength of a pairing interaction, we present a unified description of the BCS--BEC and BCS--rashbon BEC crossover phenomena.

items.title: Spectral Softening and the Structural Breakdown of Thermodynamic Equilibrium
items.summary: Reversible quasistatic thermodynamics requires normalizable instantaneous equilibrium states and dynamics allowing their attainment or tracking. We examine these requirements in a driven two-dimensional quadratic Hamiltonian with an angular-momentum coupling and a spatially uniform momentum shift $p_c(t)$, representable by a time-dependent vector potential. Its undriven part has normal-mode frequencies $ω_\pm=ω_1\pmω_2$ and the Fock--Darwin structure of a charged oscillator in a perpendicular magnetic field. At the exact soft-mode endpoint $ω_-=0$, confinement is lost in one normal-mode sector. For every strictly positive $ω_-$, the canonical Gibbs state remains normalizable; only at the endpoint does the canonical trace cease to be finite. In the quasi-soft regime, where $ω_-\to0^+$, exact adjacent-level couplings yield a dimensionless adiabatic parameter proportional to $|\dot p_c|/ω_-^2$. The standard adiabatic criterion requires this parameter to remain much smaller than unity. At a fixed occupation and a fixed nonzero driving rate, however small, this parameter grows without bound as $ω_-\to0^+$, eventually violating this criterion. In an open system, thermal tracking additionally depends on relaxation relative to the driving timescale. An explicit linear system--bath coupling illustrates why the relaxation rate cannot be inferred from the soft-mode spacing alone. Finally, the thermal Wigner function and its classical limit show that phase-space confinement is lost in both descriptions at the soft-mode endpoint. Taken together, our results show that canonical equilibrium is lost at $ω_-=0$. For $ω_->0$, the Gibbs state exists, while the ability to track it dynamically depends on the driving and dissipation.

items.title: Multilevel Quantum Dynamics: A Parafermionic Truncated Wigner Approach
items.summary: We introduce the parafermionic truncated Wigner approximation ($p$TWA), a semiclassical phase-space method for studying the nonequilibrium dynamics of multilevel quantum systems, including $\mathbb{Z}_n$ Fock parafermions. Motivated by the fractional exchange statistics of Fock parafermions, we express the Hamiltonian in a basis of local Hubbard operators that closes under commutation. This representation yields a Lie--Poisson formulation in which stochastic sampling of the initial state is followed by deterministic semiclassical evolution. We benchmark the method for single-site clock dynamics, a fully connected $\mathbb{Z}_n$ clock model that generalizes the Lipkin--Meshkov--Glick model, long-range $\mathbb{Z}_3$ clock chains, and clean and disordered one-dimensional Fock parafermion chains. The method captures qualitative features of the quantum benchmarks, including excitation spreading, disorder-induced suppression of transport, and long-time imbalance plateaus. In the single-hopping parafermion chains, it predicts slower domain-wall relaxation than time-evolving block decimation.

items.title: Landau Theory of Black Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
items.summary: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

items.title: Spontaneous axis formation through defect fusion in active nematics
items.summary: Initially spherical embryos break symmetry to establish a body axis. Topological defects in tissue nematic order have been implicated in axis formation, but the physical mechanisms underlying defect organization in active materials remain unclear. We study an active nematic fluid on a sphere using a fully covariant hydrodynamic theory that ensures thermodynamic consistency in the passive limit. We find that, in compressible systems, active nematic traction drives a spontaneous transition from the equilibrium configuration of four separated +1/2 defects to two antipodal +1 defects through pairwise fusion. The resulting state defines an axis, with aster or vortex textures at the poles depending on the flow-nematic coupling. These results identify a physical mechanism by which active forces reorganize topological defects to establish an axis on a spherical surface.

items.title: Moiré Engineering of Square-Lattice Hubbard Models for Copper- and Iron-Based Superconductors
items.summary: We propose twisted $Γ$-valley square-lattice homobilayers, exemplified by ZnF$_2$, as a tunable reference platform to emulate square lattice Hubbard-type models relevant to high-temperature superconductors. With model parameters derived from first-principles calculations, the lowest moiré band realizes a single-orbital Hubbard model underlying cuprates, while the next two realize a $p_x, p_y$ model with the minimal symmetry structure of pnictide $d_{xz}$, $d_{yz}$ Hamiltonians. Hartree-Fock analysis further predicts an antiferro-orbital ferromagnetic insulator at quarter filling.

items.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
items.summary: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative $n$-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor $p(x_n \mid x_{1:n-1})$ through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. $n$ controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter $d$ controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing $n$-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controlled approximations by using tree-grams as generative models. In particular, we show that hyperparameter transfer under $μ$P can be made more robust when narrower models are tuned on simpler data, generated by tree-grams with moderate $n$ and $d$. In addition, we show that entropy and effective range of correlations control performance gap after fine-tuning. This is because tree-grams allow us to explicitly control horizon and capacity. When allowed to route across candidate topologies, we observe emergent sparsity in tree-grams. Such concentrated routing permits pruning upto 95\% of topologies without significant change in performance.

items.title: Memory kernel and closure for systems driven by intermittent forcing with power-law waiting times
items.summary: Many systems are controlled by intermittent control variables that take on a random value for a random time interval. In the presence of such noise at update steps, the main equation for the controlled variables has a memory kernel whose coefficients are the cumulants, also known as $G$-cumulants, of the noise, which are fully ordered in time. In the case of Poisson switching, these correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the jump distribution, and the kernel can be summed exactly. We derive an exact decomposition of these coefficients for any waiting-time distribution with independent amplitudes and durations, which separates the jump statistics from the renewal statistics. In the case of waiting times that follow a power-law distribution with a finite mean, it is highly probable that a long time interval will be covered by a single period, and we have shown that, as a result, the coefficients for long delays intersect in all orders, from Boolean cumulants to the usual moments of the jump law. The long-lag kernel thus becomes a superposition of frozen deterministic flux kernels, weighted by the expression $ξ^2p(ξ)$, and from this the corresponding main equation in closed form follows. For $2<μ<3$, where the noise correlation time is infinite, the second-order closure retains a finite error even in the presence of slow dynamics, whereas the main equation of the frozen flows in this limit yields an exact stationary mean value. The telegraphic process is the only case of noise with renewal steps for which second-order conclusions are exact. An exactly solvable model with additive and correlated multiplicative noise confirms these predictions.

items.title: Ergotropy of macroscopic classical systems
items.summary: We address the fundamental question of what is the maximal amount of energy (a.k.a. ergotropy) that can be extracted from a macroscopic classical system by means of a cyclical variation of an external parameter. We show that if the system is prepared in a statistical state of the form $ρ= F(H)$, with $H$ the Hamiltonian and $F$ a generic limited function, then the ergotropy is vanishing in the {large $N$} limit, provided the thermodynamic entropy obeys the scaling $\mathcal S(E) \simeq N^αs ({E}/{N^β})$ with $α,β>0$ and $s$ some strictly increasing function with certain reasonable properties. We stress that such ubiquitous condition also ensures the equivalence of the so-called "surface" and "volume" entropies. We illustrate this by introducing the notion of ``ergotropic rearrangement'' of a phase space density which we then apply to find the exact ergotropy expression of systems with constant (positive or negative) heat capacity being evenly distributed over energy shells in phase space. We discuss cases where the above mentioned equivalence does (does not) break and the ergotropy does (does not) vanish accordingly, in the large $N$ limit. The presented results shed new light on the statistical-mechanical foundations of the second law of thermodynamics.

items.title: Quasi-long-range order in the quantum XY model on Sierpiński gaskets
items.summary: Fractal geometry has recently been shown to enhance the amplitude of the superconducting order parameter, but the fate of the superconducting phase on such lattices is far less clear. Classical XY models on finitely ramified fractals have no finite-temperature transition, as the energy of a vortex stays bounded as the system grows. However, that statement concerns an infinite gasket and thermal vortices, while real fractal structures are finite by construction. It also leaves open what happens at $T = 0$, where the phase competes not with temperature but with its own quantum fluctuations. In this work we address whether superconducting phase coherence survives at $T=0$. %Whether coherence survives those is the prior question, and the one we address here. To that end, we study the spin-$1/2$ XY ferromagnet, the phase sector of a Josephson network with at most one Cooper pair per island, thus capturing the maximum effect of quantum phase fluctuations, on both triangular and honeycomb Sierpiński gaskets. By using vision-transformer neural quantum states optimized by variational Monte Carlo, we reach generations up to $G = 5$, that is $366$ sites for the triangular gasket and $609$ for the honeycomb one, well beyond the reach of exact diagonalization. We find that the transverse two-point correlator decays algebraically, $C_{xy}(r) \sim r^{-η}$ with $η\simeq 0.12\!-\!0.32$, independent of distance measured along the graph, along the fractal boundary, or in the embedding plane. Quantum phase fluctuations thus leave quasi-long-range order intact in the ground state. We further discuss the implication of these results for the superconducting response of a finite gasket at low but nonzero temperature.

items.title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
items.summary: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

items.title: Atomic-scale Imaging of Time Reversal Breaking Supercurrents in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$
items.summary: A persistent mystery of CuO_2-based high temperature superconductivity has been the mechanism and consequences of time reversal ($\mathcal{T}$)-symmetry breaking. Although theoretical hypotheses focus upon persistent electronic currents as a potential cause, these have been invisible to direct experimental probes. That impasse has recently been removed by development of techniques for atomic-scale supercurrent visualization. Here, by imaging the energy-resolved density of electronic states $N(r,E)$ in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$, we search for the specific signatures of flowing supercurrents in a disordered $d$-wave superconductor. Employing the strategy of artificial neural networks (ANN) for complex quantum matter visualization, we designed a dual-ANN (VMAP) to efficiently implement $d$-wave supercurrent visualization, achieving imaging of supercurrent speeds $V(r)$ at magnetic fields $|B| \leq μT$ in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$. Correspondence between specific characteristics of $N(r,E)$ around each supercurrent loop and a quantum "Rosetta Stone" which translates $N(r,E)$ to $V(r)$, emphasizes the validity of $V(r)$ detection and visualization. Then, for hole-densities 0.17 $\leq p \leq$ 0.22 we observe statistically repeatable networks of supercurrent flows. Crucially, these supercurrents satisfy Kirchhoff's law at junctions within each network. Further, theoretical predictions for supercurrent speeds $V$ in disordered $d$-wave superconductors are consistent with measured 1250 m/s $< V <$ 4000 m/s, and with reported magnetic field amplitudes $|B| \approx$ 0.1 mT Thus, detection and visualization of these supercurrent loop networks provides unique perspectives on $\mathcal{T}$-symmetry breaking in cuprates. It also emphasizes the accelerating utility of ANN techniques for physics discovery from high data volume quantum matter research.

items.title: Reversing the text is not reversing the path: a fixed-text measure without a zero, and an assembly-order comparison that vanishes identically
items.summary: For an ensemble of trajectories the fluctuation theorems give the entropy production its meaning and zero. The same expression has recently been evaluated on one fixed text, $Δ= [\log P(x) - \log P(\tilde x)]/L$ with $\tilde x$ the text in reversed order, read as an entropy production separating causally from arbitrarily ordered prose. A single text is neither a distribution nor a dynamics, and the texts at issue were produced by other models. No theorem fixes where the zero of a fixed-text quantity lies: the expression carries over from an ensemble, its zero does not. We supply a zero from an exact antisymmetry. Scoring a text's $n$ sentences in all $n!$ orders, reversal carries $π$ to $π\circ \mathrm{rev}$, a measure-preserving involution, so $Δ(π) = -Δ(π\circ \mathrm{rev})$ identically and the values are centred at zero for any score. The authored arrangement's midrank is then unitless, bounded, and 0.50 for a score blind to order. Across five autoregressive evaluators from 124M to 4B parameters, and taking the prompt-defined labels at face value, 8% to 15% of the median midrank's distance from the null is attributable to causal order and the rest to the arrangement being the order the passage was produced in. The thermodynamic reading needs a comparison whose zero does hold on the text read, and a masked model supplies one: the any-order chain rule gives a genuine log-probability, and its left-to-right and right-to-left orders for one text give $σ$, a comparison of two assembly orders. Both run from the empty sequence to the same text, so it is not a path against its time reverse. It vanishes identically when the evaluator's conditionals come from a joint, and a non-zero reading reports the evaluator's incompatibility, not the text. Neither is a fixed-text entropy production, for different reasons.

items.title: Predictive beam-lattice reduction for higher-order topological modes in a 2D SSH phononic crystal
items.summary: We develop a mechanically faithful reduced model for a two-dimensional topological phononic crystal composed of rigid square masses connected by slender elastic ligaments. Exploiting Euler Bernoulli beam theory, we derive a Hermitian 12 degree of freedom dynamical matrix that retains in-plane translations, rotations, and ligament eccentricity. This reduction captures effects that are absent from scalar mass spring SSH models while remaining computationally much more tractable and more easily interpretable than full finite element simulations. Dimerizing the ligament widths produces a mechanical 2D SSH lattice with a full band gap and a quantized bulk polarization. The sign of the dimerization controls the transition from trivial to non trivial phases, while ligament eccentricity provides an additional purely geometric mechanism for changing the topology. Ribbon and finite cell calculations predict in gap edge and corner modes, quantified by localization measures and confirmed by finite element simulations. Measurements on 3D printed samples show an evanescent response in the trivial structure and enhanced boundary/corner response in the non trivial structure within the predicted gap. The results provide a validated route for designing topological elastic metamaterials using a continuum informed discrete model rather than either idealized mass spring networks or brute force numerical optimization.

items.title: Spin and Orbital Angular Momentum Textures at Chiral Molecule-Metal Interfaces
items.summary: Chiral molecular adsorption can modify the spin and orbital character of metal surface states, providing an electronic-structure basis for interpreting spin-dependent interfacial phenomena. Using first-principles calculations with spin-orbit coupling, band unfolding, and an atom-projected orbital angular momentum (OAM) analysis, we investigate spin and OAM textures at chiral heptahelicene/Au(111) interfaces and compare them with clean Au (111) and an achiral coronene/Au system. Adsorption changes the orientations of the spin and OAM vectors and reduces the sampled OAM magnitudes of Au-derived surface states near the Fermi level. The two heptahelicene enantiomers exhibit textures related by mirror and time-reversal symmetries, whereas the comparison with coronene identifies changes that also occur without molecular chirality. These results clarify how molecular adsorption modifies interfacial spin and orbital character and establish symmetry constraints relevant to chirality-dependent photoemission.

items.title: Ab initio Engineering of Topological Superconductivity in Substrate-Supported Magnetic Chains
items.summary: In this paper, we employ a combination of several first-principles-based approaches to systematically scan chains of several types of magnetic atoms in different chain geometries on top of various overlayers on the Nb(110) surface, to develop a pathway to engineer topological Majorana edge states. Using atomistic spin-model calculations, we first identify a rich variety of magnetic configurations, including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, spin-spiral, and exotic up-up-down-down states stabilized solely within a second-order Heisenberg model. In the next step, we solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations using a band-theoretical method. Depending on the magnetic structure and atomic configuration, the superconducting spectra may exhibit topologically trivial minigaps, broad overlapping Shiba bands, or localized zero-energy edge states accompanied by sizable topological minigaps. In particular, Fe chains on Ag/Nb(110) are found to display pronounced signatures associated with topological superconductivity, including strongly localized zero-energy edge states and indications of Shiba band inversion. We further demonstrate that changes in the spin structure or a small amount of spatial relaxation can substantially modify the superconducting band structure and the localization properties of the edge states.

items.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. II. A path-probability formalism
items.summary: We develop a dynamical theory of the East model---a one-dimensional, hierarchically constrained kinetic Ising model---based on path-probability densities. This theory yields an infinite but closed set of equations for single-spin path-probability densities, which, after Laplace transformation, become algebraic difference equations. To render the theory tractable, we introduce a systematic factorization approximation in which the joint probability densities of consecutive flip intervals are factorized into lower-order joint probability densities. We implement the first-order single-interval factorization approximation, obtain a closed set of four equations for the persistence functions, and solve them numerically. The resulting time correlation functions and relaxation times agree closely with Monte Carlo simulations and with the two-domain-basis approximation of the Zwanzig--Mori formalism over a wide range of temperatures, although both approximations fail to capture the exact low-temperature asymptotic super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time. The present formalism provides a plausible foundation for a complete and rigorous theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model and offers a promising route toward generalization to other systems.

items.title: Indentation of pre-tensioned cortex-like fibre networks: tension, local stretching and the signature of defect architecture
items.summary: Indentation is widely used to infer the mechanical state of biological materials like the actomyosin cortex. It reduces a single force-indentation curve to an apparent modulus. The cortex, however, is a pre-tensioned, heterogeneous fibre network. We show that this inference is ambiguous. The same amount of weakening can leave the indentation force unchanged or lower it tenfold, depending on where it lies relative to the probe. The force reflects how the probe couples to the tensioned, load-bearing structure, not the amount of weakening. We combine molecular dynamics simulations of a pressure-loaded, crosslinked fibre network indented by a rigid sphere with a continuum membrane solution. We represent the simulated force-depth response by a two-term fit, $F\propto aδ+bδ^{3/2}$, with $a$ reflecting the global tension, and $b$ the stiffening with depth. At a fixed fraction of weakened bonds, diffuse weakening lowers the force by a factor of about 1.5. A weak cluster beneath the probe lowers it 8-12-fold, because the slack cluster decouples the probe from the tension. When the clusters are displaced from the contact, the force returns to within 15% of the healthy value. Two opposite effects cancel. The clusters soften the whole layer, which lowers its tension and the force. But they also channel the load through the intact network beneath the probe, which stiffens it locally and raises the force. The shape of the curve retains what the force level hides. The coefficient $a$ reflects the softened layer when clusters beside the probe keep the force near the healthy value. The local exponent $α=\mathrm{d}\ln F/\mathrm{d}\lnδ$ increases with depth in every configuration except when a cluster lies beneath the probe, where the two-term form no longer applies. Detecting localised weakening requires spatial sampling and analysis of the curve shape, not a single fitted modulus.

items.title: Strange-Metal Magnetotransport without a Strange-Metal Ground State
items.summary: Strange metals display a linear-in-temperature resistivity, $ρ_{xx}\sim T$, and a quadratic inverse Hall angle, $\cotΘ_H\sim T^2$. These seemingly universal laws are often attributed to quantum criticality, yet no controlled theory realizes both at an asymptotic zero-temperature fixed point, and experimentally they persist only over finite temperature windows. Here, we show that these properties can arise from an intermediate critical regime that does not govern the ground state. Using a minimal class of holographic models, we construct a fully backreacted realization of both scalings, which appear within a finite temperature window controlled by an emergent intermediate scaling geometry. The window is bounded by relevant deformations of the corresponding fixed point: momentum relaxation sets the upper edge, while the magnetic field $B$ closes it from below at $T_{\min}\sim B^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic corrections. At $T_{\min}$, strange-metal transport, the scaling geometry, and critical thermodynamics break down together. Our results point to intermediate criticality as a distinct route to strange-metal transport, and suggest that it can be identified by the simultaneous breakdown of transport and thermodynamic scaling under a magnetic field.

items.title: Quasiconformal geometry and elastic anisotropy in liquid crystals
items.summary: Unequal splay and bend elastic constants endow planar nematic liquid crystals with a director-dependent anisotropic geometry. Here, we show that this geometry is quasiconformal: the magnitude of the associated Beltrami coefficient is fixed by the elastic constants, while its phase depends on the director relative to a compatible rotating frame introducing an SO(2) spin connection. We construct explicit maps for a hybrid-aligned film and isolated defect textures, generalizing the conformal construction of isotropic defects. These results provide a new insight into the classical Dzyaloshinskii defect solutions, which are shown to define an auxiliary reference cone on which the defect texture is quasiconformally distorted before being projected conformally into physical space. Numerical simulations of constrained +2 defects reveal core morphologies consistent with the quasiconformal geometry. Our results suggest that quasiconformal maps provide a broader geometric language for anisotropy in liquid crystals and other materials.

items.title: Polymer adsorption on vicinal surfaces
items.summary: While polymer adsorption is theoretically well established on flat surfaces --- and somewhat understood on rough surfaces --- the common and practically relevant case of nearly flat stepped surfaces remains poorly studied. Here, we address this gap via extensive simulations of flexible polymer chains grafted at the step edge of vicinal surfaces. For wide terraces, the polymer-step interaction yields a stable step-attached (SA) phase, alongside the desorbed and terrace-adsorbed (TA) phases, all of them separated by continuous transition lines that meet at a multicritical point previously unanticipated in polymer thermodynamics. This scenario is observed for terrace widths $\mathcal{W} \gtrsim 3 R_g^{(2D)}$, being $R_g^{(2D)}$ the radius of gyration of TA polymers. Simpler phase diagrams, absent this multicriticality, are found for $\mathcal{W} \lesssim 3 R_g^{(2D)}$, where a simple crossover exists between the SA and TA phases. The presence of kinks at the steps does not alter these behaviors. Besides their theoretical relevance, these findings unveil an interesting route to produce polymer nanowires and control polymer conformation via step attachment-detachment on designed stepped surfaces.

items.title: Observation of far-from-equilibrium scaling in the transient dynamics of 2D quantum magnets
items.summary: The transient regime of far-from-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics lacks the established organizing principles that universality and scaling provide in equilibrium. It is least understood for two-dimensional short-range interacting systems, where mean-field arguments are not expected to hold, controlled theoretical descriptions are few, and fluctuations are strong. Here we investigate the quench dynamics of the transverse-field Ising model using programmable Rydberg-atom arrays realizing honeycomb, square, kagome, and triangular lattices.
