items.title: Intelligent hydrovoltaic actuation with proactive ion regulation during solar desalination
items.summary: ABSTRACT Solar desalination offers a sustainable approach to freshwater generation, yet it is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation at evaporation interfaces. While common salt-rejecting strategies can mitigate macroscopic fouling, they fail to achieve real-time monitoring and active management of salts at the metastable stage. Local ion enrichment and associated pre-crystallization processes will degrade efficiency through increased mass-transfer resistance and vaporization enthalpy. Herein, we propose active salt management as a proactive system function and fabricate an intelligent dynamic evaporator (IDE) that integrates in-situ sensing, adaptive decision-making, and active regulation. The asymmetrically oxidized PPy/cotton is applied for real-time monitoring of ion concentration evolution within nanochannels via hydrovoltaic actuation. Coupled with deep learning algorithms, IDE dynamically correlates electrical outputs with salt enrichment states, enabling advanced intervention before critical accumulation. Dynamic solar tracking enables uniform interfacial evaporation and ion enrichment, elevating the stability of hydrovoltaic potential signals and the recognition precision (93.8%) of salt enrichment states. Overall, radiation-adaptive and self-cleaning IDE delivers an average daily freshwater production of 12.3 kg m −2 over 100 days. This work shifts salt management from static material design to intelligent adaptive control, providing a scalable framework for robust and sustainable water purification.

items.title: Van der Waals-modulated integration strategy unlocks scalable fabrication of high-density organic electronic and optoelectronic devices
items.summary: Abstract The advancement of organic electronics and optoelectronics fundamentally depends on the development of high-precision integration technologies. However, existing manufacturing approaches for organic semiconductors, particularly conventional photolithography and stencil lithography, are plagued by an intractable trade-off between integration density and device performance. Here we report a van der Waals (vdW)-modulated integration strategy that circumvents this long-standing bottleneck, enabling concurrent high-density and high-performance organic devices. By tailoring the surface chemistry of an ultrathin Parylene shadow mask, we precisely tune interfacial vdW interactions to orchestrate deterministic mask manipulation and high-fidelity patterning. Consequently, organic field-effect transistor (OFET) arrays achieve a device density of 2,500 transistors cm −2 with an average on-state current density of 1.20 μA μm −1 , among the highest reported for integrated organic electronics. Furthermore, this strategy is extended to monolithic OFET-organic light-emitting diode (OLED) integration, yielding efficient light-emitting transistor arrays. This work establishes an integration route that preserves the organic semiconductor interface while avoiding direct photolithographic contact with the active layer, opening a route toward large-scale, multifunctional organic integrated systems.

items.title: Spontaneous N-formylation of amines with carbon monoxide in irradiated water
items.summary: Abstract N -formyl amines are crucial synthetic intermediates, yet their production often relies on methods requiring precious metal catalysts, suffering from activation barrier or generating stoichiometric waste. Concurrently, the astrochemical origin of formamide, a prebiotic precursor, remains debated. Herein, we report a catalyst-free, radical-driven N -formylation strategy that addresses both challenges. Using only water as the solvent and X-ray or electron beam as the energy source, we achieve efficient coupling between carbon monoxide (CO) and amines under ambient conditions. Scaling up with a high-flux electron beam delivers a formamide production rate of 0.35 ± 0.01 mmol L −1 min −1 , with favorable techno-economic analysis indicating industrial potential. The reaction proceeds via the in-situ generation of key radicals ( • CHO from CO and • NR 1 R 2 from amines) generated by species (e aq − , • H, • OH) produced during water radiolysis, followed by spontaneous C–N coupling. This method exhibits superior C–N coupling reactivity for most derivatives including electron-donating and electron-withdrawing group and achieves a notable radiation-chemical yield up to 4.6 × 10 −7 mol J −1 . Beyond synthesis, this work may offer mechanistic insights into the related radiation-driven prebiotic pathway, demonstrating that radiolysis of simple mixtures (H 2 O, CO, NH 3 ) can efficiently yield formamide, thereby bridging green chemistry and astrochemistry.

items.title: Symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient CO2 electroreduction in strong acidic media
items.summary: Abstract Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in strong acidic media (pH ≤ 2) offers many unique advantages compared to alkaline electrolytes, but it still remains some significant challenges including the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), low selectivity and poor stability. Herein, we report that symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites incorporated within ultrathin covalent organic polymer nanosheets (p-Ni 1/2 Pc), can simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient acidic CO 2 RR. Direct visualization via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the presence of Ni vacancies and uncoordinated pyrrolic N, which collectively break the local symmetry around Ni sites. This asymmetry not only optimizes the electronic structure of Ni sites to kinetically favor CO 2 RR over HER, but more importantly, it reconfigures the interfacial hydrogen-bond network via uncoordinated pyrrolic N. The reconstructed hydrogen-bond network effectively restricts proton transfer, while symmetry breaking creates a CO 2 -enriched local microenvironment. Consequently, p-Ni 1/2 Pc catalyst exhibits a remarkable 97.5% CO Faraday efficiency (FE) and a maximum 402.9 mA cm −2 partial current density ( j CO ) in strong acidic electrolytes (pH = 1), while maintaining stable operation for 85 h without salt precipitation. This work highlights the critical role of symmetry-breaking in simultaneously engineering active sites and interfacial microenvironments for robust CO 2 RR in acidic media.

items.title: Thermal-fluctuator-driven decoherence of an oscillator near-resonantly coupled to a two-level system
authors: Thomas J Antolin, Jonas Glatthard and Andrew D Armour
items.summary: Recent experiments on a range of engineered quantum systems have highlighted the important role of interacting two-level systems (TLSs) in modifying device properties and generating fluctuations. Focusing on the case of an oscillator coupled to a single near-resonant TLS, we explore how interactions between the TLS and lower-frequency thermally activated two-level fluctuators (TLFs) degrade the oscillator’s coherence. Depending on the strength of the couplings, a single TLF can give rise to coherence oscillations that appear alongside, or supplant, Rabi oscillations of the oscillator–TLS system. Bath-driven transitions in the TLF cause irreversible coherence decay at a rate that is highly sensitive to both the couplings and the transition rate. For an ensemble of TLFs, we identify and characterise the different regimes of non-exponential phase-averaging-driven coherence decay that the oscillator can display. Using numerical calculations, we examine the extent to which systems with just a few TLFs differ from the limit of a large (continuum) TLF ensemble. Our work provides a theoretical framework for understanding the interplay of coherent TLS interactions and TLF-induced dephasing in quantum devices such as superconducting and phononic resonators.

items.title: Sensitive Thermometry with a Fiber-Integrated Optical Microcavity
authors: Min She, 敏 佘, Qiang Zhang, 强 张, Zhao An, 钊 安, Fan Lv, 帆 吕, Zhaoyi Liu, 兆亿 刘, Jitao Cao, 济韬 曹, Yuhong Zou, 榆红 邹, Ruikai Pan, 瑞恺 潘, Wenpeng Zhou, 文鹏 周, Han Zhang, 涵 张, Jiangshan Tang, 江山 唐, Feng Wang, 峰 王, Franco Nori, Keyu Xia and 可宇 夏
items.summary: High-sensitivity thermometry is critical for cutting-edge technologies such as gravimeters, quantum clocks, and lithography systems. Although recent transformative advances in resonator-based optical microthermometers achieve high sensitivity, the input and output setups are complex and require precise control, severely limiting their practical applications and achievable footprint. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a fiber-integrated thermometer made of a high-Q optical Fabry–Pérot fiber microcavity, filled with transparent but thermal-sensitive ultraviolet glue. The input and transmitted probe laser fields are coupled to the microthermometer via optical fibers, significantly facilitating operation and minimizing the device size. Combining the large temperature dependence of the ultraviolet glue and the micrometer-scale cavity, sensitive thermometry is achieved by independently measuring the resonance shift or the transmission change. Based on evaluation of equivalent temperature noise of the power spectral density, the resonance-shift method achieves microkelvin-level sensitivity. The fixed-wavelength transmission-change method yields a nanokelvin-level readout-referred equivalent temperature-noise floor at high frequencies using quasi-static response calibration. This low-cost, simple, and fiber-integrated microthermometer holds significant potential for applications in quantum device characterization, biocalorimetry, optoelectronic technologies, and next-generation clocks.

items.title: Double Cavity Exceptional-Point Enhanced Laser Cooling of Semiconductors
authors: Haonan Chang, 浩男 常, Feilong Song, 飞龙 宋, Jun Zhang and 俊 张
items.summary: Laser cooling of semiconductors requires a high external quantum efficiency for phonon-assisted upconversion while suppressing heat generated by background absorption and non-radiative relaxation. Nanophotonic resonances can strengthen the upconversion channel, but in a single-mode structure may also enhance parasitic pump heating. We introduce a two-cavity non-Hermitian architecture that separates preparation of a lower reservoir state from extraction of the phonon-promoted radiative state. A passive exceptional point, containing no optical gain, is placed in the output branch, where it reshapes the projected final-state optical response; all anti-Hermitian diagonal terms describe radiative leakage, internal absorption, or material decay. For a CdS parameter set, the four-mode calculation gives a 1.23 × 103 enhancement of upconverted photoluminescence relative to a single-mode control, while the pump-induced heat load rises by only 2.8 × 10–3%. The gain consists of a factor of 3.45 × 102 from the independent output resonance and a further factor of 3.56 from exceptional-point tuning.

items.title: Interference-Controlled Nonclassical Photon Emission via Cavity-Mediated Spin Exchange
items.summary: The generation of nonclassical light with strong photon antibunching and appreciable brightness remains an important goal in quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate that cavity-mediated spin-exchange interactions provide a route to overcome this constraint by amplifying spectral anharmonicity. In a two-emitter cavity-QED system with a controllable relative phase ϕ, the resulting interference–interaction mechanism reshapes the dressed-state manifold and enables switching between distinct quantum emission regimes. For ϕ = 0, constructive interference yields high-quality single-photon emission with near-perfect antibunching, suppressing by more than three orders of magnitude while maintaining a substantial intracavity photon population. Conversely, for ϕ =π, destructive interference suppresses direct single-photon excitation and selectively enhances two-photon excitation, producing signatures of correlated two-photon emission with appreciable intracavity photon populations and suppressed higher-order excitations. Our work establishes interference-engineered interactions as a mechanism for the controllable selection of single-photon and photon-pair emission, opening new opportunities for programmable nonclassical light sources and quantum photonic applications.

items.title: Pulse-Controlled Topologically Protected Quantum Batteries
authors: Jin Yang, 瑾 杨, Biao Xiong, 标 熊, Jibing Liu, 继兵 刘, Houguo Yu, 厚果 余, Dehua Liu, 德华 刘, Feng Mei, 锋 梅, Chuanjia Shan and 传家 单
items.summary: Remote charging in the field of quantum batteries is particularly appealing because it minimizes interference between the charger and the battery, making it a subject of considerable interest. Here, we propose a robust remote charging protocol for quantum batteries based on a pulse-controlled superconducting qubit chain. By dynamically modulating the pulse-mediated couplings, we realize chiral-symmetry-protected energy transfer from the charger to the battery. We show that the charging process suppresses energy backflow due to the pulse control and remains robust against pulse imperfections due to the chiral symmetry of the system. Moreover, the energy stored in the battery at the target time is almost fully extractable, and the protocol remains effective over a moderate range of chain lengths. To further accelerate charging, we optimize the pulse shape and elucidate the underlying physical mechanism. Our pulse-controlled topological quantum battery protocol provides a versatile framework for implementing remote topological charging and establishes a theoretical foundation for designing optimal-control strategies to enhance quantum battery performance.

items.title: Switchable Auxetic Piezoelectricity in Rhombohedral Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: He-Meng Sun, 和猛 孙, Hang-Bo Zhang, 杭波 张, Zhi Tan, 智 谭, Ming-Min Yang and 明敏 杨
items.summary: Piezoelectric materials typically exhibit opposite longitudinal and transverse mechanical responses under an electric field, reflecting the electromechanical analogue of a positive Poisson’s ratio. Auxetic piezoelectricity, in which longitudinal and transverse coefficients share the same sign, has recently emerged as an unconventional electromechanical response; yet its intrinsic realization and electrical tunability in relaxor ferroelectrics with complex domain structures remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate intrinsic and electrically switchable auxetic piezoelectricity in rhombohedral relaxor ferroelectric Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-PbTiO3 by combining first-principles calculations and quantitative piezoelectric measurements. Density functional perturbation theory reveals that a positive transverse piezoelectric response is symmetry-allowed in the rhombohedral phase and primarily originates from internal-strain contributions associated with cooperative Pb-O displacements. Experiments on single-domain (111)pc-oriented crystals confirm the existence of an intrinsic auxetic state. Beyond the single-domain limit, in situ bias-dependent measurements reveal continuous and reversible electric-field-driven switching between auxetic and conventional piezoelectric states within the same crystal. A tensor-rotation-based multi-domain model quantitatively reproduces the bias-dependent response and identifies domain redistribution, enabled by the large shear piezoelectric coefficient, as the microscopic origin of the switching behavior. These findings establish auxetic piezoelectricity as an intrinsic and electrically programmable response in rhombohedral relaxor ferroelectrics, providing a general route toward reconfigurable electromechanical functionalities.

items.title: Beyond Classical Nucleation: Density-Controlled Relaxation Mechanism in Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
authors: Yue Shan, 月 单, Pengfei Zhang, 朋飞 张, Chun-Lai Ren, 春来 任, Yu-Qiang Ma and 余强 马
items.summary: A recent experiment [Natl. Sci. Rev. 13 nwag107 (2026)] revealed a density transition during nucleation of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), yet its physical origin remains unresolved. Here, using minimal coarse-grained sticker–spacer models, we identify a density-controlled relaxation mechanism governing nucleation under weak multivalent interactions. This mechanism emerges across three hierarchical levels. At the cluster level, nucleation proceeds via reversible, density-regulated nuclei beyond classical nucleation theory. At the molecular level, the configurational distributions of chains within nucleating clusters evolve non-monotonically with cluster size relative to those of isolated single chains, while their conformational fluctuations exhibit exponential relaxation with a characteristic timescale ( ). At the bond level, reversible bond turnover accelerates with cluster growth, yielding a characteristic aggregation number (N *) that marks density saturation and the onset of irreversible growth. The correspondence between and N * reveals that nucleation is intrinsically governed by relaxation dynamics. These results establish density-controlled bond turnover as a key kinetic regulator of IDP nucleation and provide a general framework for phase transitions driven by weak multivalent interactions.

items.title: Coherent high-velocity chiral magnons in the metallic altermagnet CrSb
items.summary: Altermagnets combine the zero net magnetization of antiferromagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting, creating new opportunities for spintronic and magnonic technologies. The full realization of this promise necessitates a material that is simultaneously metallic and altermagnetic, yet preserves the long magnon lifetimes more often seen in insulators. Here, we use polarized neutron diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering to determine the magnetic structure and spin dynamics of the metallic altermagnet CrSb. We confirm a fully compensated, collinear magnetic structure with localized Cr moments and establish the microscopic spin Hamiltonian governing its excitations. Despite its metallicity, CrSb hosts remarkably coherent magnons across its 230 meV bandwidth, with group velocities approaching 60 km/s. Along low-symmetry momentum directions, we resolve chiral magnon splitting generated by higher-order, symmetry-inequivalent exchange interactions, providing the first experimental observation of this phenomenon in a metallic altermagnet. These results reveal a nearly complete separation between magnetic and electronic degrees of freedom in CrSb and demonstrate that metallic transport, room-temperature altermagnetic order, fast coherent magnons, and chiral spin dynamics can coexist in a single material, positioning CrSb as a compelling platform for spintronic applications.

items.title: Enhanced Multifractality Induced by Non-Hermitian Disorder in Quantum Percolation
items.summary: We study the two-dimensional quantum site-percolation model with reciprocal hopping and random imaginary on-site potentials, which describe spatially uncorrelated gain and loss. The localization properties of the eigenstates are characterized through the complex spacing ratio, the participation entropy, and the generalized fractal dimensions $D_q$. Finite-size scaling yields an effective quantum percolation threshold $p_q$ that increases monotonically with $γ$, with a shift larger than that produced by a real on-site potential of equal strength. We show that the onset of extended behavior drifts toward larger occupation probabilities as the system size increases. The localization--delocalization change is therefore a crossover, consistent with the absence of a sharp transition for reciprocal non-Hermitian disorder in two dimensions. Accordingly, the interval between the classical threshold $p_c$ and $p_q$ constitutes an extended multifractal crossover regime and its width at accessible sizes grows with $γ$. Although all states are expected to localize in the thermodynamic limit, above $p_q$ the localization length exceeds the largest system size simulated, which is already larger than current photonic samples. The size-dependent threshold and the multifractal regime, which widens with the loss strength and can therefore be reached without fine-tuning, are thus directly accessible in photonic waveguide lattices.

items.title: Structural balance in complex networks: from measurement to dynamics, emergence and implications
items.summary: Structural balance theory, introduced in social psychology to describe how friendly and hostile ties organize into consistent patterns, has been reinterpreted through statistical physics and complex networks. In the classical formulation, a triad with positive or negative links, representing friendship and hostility, is balanced when the product of its signs is positive; a balanced network splits into at most two internally friendly, mutually hostile groups. This review synthesizes how the triadic formulation has been extended to a statistical-ensemble perspective in which balance is encoded by immanent three-body interactions described by a proper Hamiltonian, balanced configurations correspond to low-energy states, and balance measures serve as order parameters for transitions between consensus, polarization, and disorder. We organize the field into three sections: Measurement, Dynamics and Emergence, and Implications. In Measurement, we compare measures of structural balance and null models, and show that conclusions for a given system depend on the chosen measure and null model. In Dynamics and Emergence, we review deterministic and stochastic systems, including the gradient, Hamiltonian, and local triad models, and examine how noise, topology, and competing mechanisms determine whether balance emerges. In Implications, we survey consequences for belief formation, opinion contagion dynamics, polarization, international relations, and markets. Across domains, the evidence is strongest for local triadic stability and weakest for system-wide balance. Balance is not synonymous with harmony: balanced structures can reflect cohesion, polarization, or persistent conflict. Its empirical relevance is well supported in some reciprocal social systems, but remains less settled in biological and other complex networks.

items.title: Mixture of Polyconvex Neural Potentials for Parametric Hyperelasticity: Towards Foundation Material Models
items.summary: Hyperelastic constitutive models enable modeling large deformations in elastic solids. In common practice, a strain energy density function is prescribed in advance and model-specific parameters are calibrated from experiments. However, many applications require constitutive models for a family of related materials whose mechanical behavior varies with composition. A fixed constitutive model-form may not capture the full range of behavior across the family, while fitting separate forms does not provide a direct way to predict the response of new compositions. Recent work has developed data-driven constitutive models that learn flexible strain energy functions while incorporating key physical constraints. In this work, we propose using mixtures of convex neural potentials based on input convex neural networks as a modular and data efficient approach to modeling material families. Each potential is convex and monotonic with respect to polyconvex strain invariants, while a conditioning network maps material descriptors to mixture weights. We compare the approach with a monolithic partially input-convex neural network using experimental data from PolyJet 3D-printed materials and a synthetic Gent-type benchmark. Across both benchmarks, the mixture architecture generalized better to material descriptors not seen during training. In the PolyJet experimental benchmark, we showed that the mixture architecture is less sensitive to model hyperparameters, while in the Gent-type benchmark it generalized more reliably with sparse data in the material-descriptor space. These results suggest that representing a material family through a small set of shared convex neural potentials provides a useful structural prior for learning descriptor-dependent constitutive behavior from limited data.

items.title: Bandwidth-tunable thermal emitter via dynamic resonator coupling and loss
items.summary: We demonstrate a dynamically tunable omnidirectional thermal emitter that can be switched from a narrowband emission state to a broadband state. The structure is a metal-backed multilayer with subwavelength thickness across the mid-infrared, which forms an angle-insensitive (up to 60°) optical cavity with one input port. We used an ultrathin VO2 layer to dynamically switch the coupling and loss coefficients of this optical cavity, resulting in narrowband emission from the vibrational mode of a polar dielectric layer that is part of the multilayer stack when the VO2 is in its insulating phase, and broadband emission from a nearly impedance-matched cavity when the VO2 is switched to its lossy metallic phase. We fabricated the structure around a free-standing silicon membrane and integrated it onto a printed circuit board (PCB), which enabled electrical switching of the emitter at the ten-to-hundred millisecond scale, and can be used for free-space identification, tagging, or communication.

items.title: Optical characterization of Fermi polarons in monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride
items.summary: Amorphous silicon nitride is the leading low-loss, CMOS-compatible platform for wafer-scale integrated photonics. Encapsulating transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers within this platform offers a promising route towards scalable TMD-photonic circuits. Yet the effect of this amorphous dielectric on the optical response of the monolayer remains poorly understood. Here, we compare monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride with a hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated reference, using differential reflectivity and photoluminescence. Whereas the reference is dominated by the neutral exciton, the nitride-encapsulated monolayer shows attractive and repulsive polaron resonances separated by ${\sim}31$~meV, with emission dominated by the attractive branch. A quantitative comparison of temperature-dependent reflectance with a microscopic finite-temperature Fermi-polaron theory shows that the nitride induces substantial electron doping in the monolayer, with an electron density of $(0.8$--$0.9)\times10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$. Using the extracted density and trion binding energy as the only input parameters, the theory reproduces the photoluminescence spectra up to ${\sim}80$ K in excellent quantitative agreement with experiments, thus corroborating the Fermi-polaron description of the observed excitonic response.

items.title: Ultrafast imprinting of fused ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic skyrmions
items.summary: Antiferromagnetic skyrmions are promising topologically protected entities for robust storage and THz transport of information. Their generation has so far relied on slow techniques or on specific magnetic structures, which limit their integration into spintronic devices. Here, we demonstrate the imprinting of antiferromagnetic skyrmions within a few picoseconds in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer with a thermal laser pulse. We identify a threshold energy required to initiate the fused skyrmion phase and show that this can be modulated by a magnetic field, enabling deterministic nucleation of antiferromagnetic skyrmions. Compared to conventional slow field-cooling processes to control antiferromagnets we show that laser-induced skyrmion imprinting can be orders of magnitude faster and provides an experimentally feasible route towards ultrafast creation and manipulation of antiferromagnetic skyrmions.

items.title: Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$: from disorder through $2\times2$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order to stripe order
items.summary: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

items.title: quantEM: Quantitative Electron Microscopy Analysis from Differentiable Physics to Neural Priors
items.summary: Quantitative electron microscopy includes imaging, diffraction, spectroscopy, and tomography measurements, and the analysis of these measurements increasingly requires solving inverse problems with physical forward models. Open-source software has made many of these analyses widely available, but most packages are organized around a single modality, so that multimodal analyses require moving data between packages, and new methods cannot easily reuse the physical models and optimizers of existing ones. Here we present quantEM, an open-source Python package for quantitative electron microscopy that uses PyTorch tensors for computation and automatic differentiation, and Zarr for storage. We implement each analysis method by writing a differentiable forward model and choosing a representation, loss function, constraints, and optimizer from a library of components, so that every method runs on CPUs and GPUs, can be saved and resumed, and uses the same calibrated data structures and visualization tools. We describe the current modules, including orientation and strain mapping, direct and iterative ptychography, tomography with neural representations, and X-ray and electron energy-loss spectroscopy, and show how we assemble combined methods such as ptychographic tomography from existing components. quantEM is available under the MIT license, together with documentation, tutorials, and curated example datasets.

items.title: Dynamics and transport in LiF using classical and machine learned interatomic potentials
items.summary: We perform molecular dynamics simulations of molten Lithium Fluoride, comparing the classical Buckingham and Born-Huggins-Mayer potentials with machine-learnt interatomic potentials - the MACE-MP-0b3 (small) foundation model potential, and a fine-tuned version thereof. We find that the MACE-MP-0b3, out-of-the-box, is able to accurately reproduce the experimental shear viscosity across the liquid state comparable with polarisable potentials despite not itself being polarisable. Previous viscosities computed using classical potentials are under-predicted, which has previously been attributed to a suppressed melting temperature. Prompted by this we compare the melting points of these potentials. We find that the machine-learnt potentials address the significant underestimation of the melting point of the classical potentials, though the refined potential and the foundation model differ significantly between themselves. We probe the microscopic structure and dynamics of each model to further elucidate the considerable change in viscosity between classical and machine-learnt potentials. We find that, despite their lower melting temperature, classical potentials produce considerably stiffer, higher frequency, single-particle and collective charge-transport dynamics on account of their fixed charges. However, in the long-wavelength limit, the many-body machine-learnt potentials feature more elastic collective motion that governs the diffusion of momentum and is therefore responsible for the enhanced shear viscosity.

items.title: Functional Compression as Occam's Razor: Algebraic Complexity from Sensitivity Minimization
items.summary: Discovering discrete algebraic structures from data is a fundamental challenge in machine learning. We ask how continuous learning objectives can favor functional compression---representing data through shared algebraic composition rather than low-rank representations. We analyze the global optima of a canonical factorization model for algebraic completion (recovering finite binary operations) that demonstrated a preference for group operations. We measure algebraic complexity by the infimum of parameter sensitivity under exact reconstruction. We establish a universal complexity floor, whose attainment forces geometric alignment and unitarity of the latent representations. At the floor, input representations compose into the corresponding output representations; their reuse across the operation table propagates these local identities to enforce a globally shared algebraic structure. If the floor is not attained, a positive gap separates it from the feasible infimum. For cancellative operations, floor attainment forces the model's latent representation to be an injective homomorphism, equivalent to the target being isotopic to a group. In this case, every global minimizer is equivalent to the underlying group's unitary left-regular representation, up to isotopy and unitary gauge, resolving the central conjecture of Huh (2025). For non-cancellative operations, floor attainment forces exact structural redundancies (identical rows or columns) and is equivalent to a unitary factorization of the target's row- and column-reduced table with orthonormal output matrices, yielding the fewest distinct input matrices compatible with exact reconstruction. The resulting cancellative table then embeds in a group-isotope table. This analysis reveals a structural bias toward functional compression: at the sensitivity floor, algebraic composition of latent representations implements the target operation.

items.title: Magnetic tuning of odd elastic instabilities in chiral active crystals
items.summary: We investigate the dynamical properties of an odd active crystal whose elementary units follow an inertial dynamics and experience a Lorentz force induced by an external magnetic field. The continuous injection of energy associated with active chirality gives rise to odd elasticity, manifested through transverse forces between the crystal constituents. We show that the interplay between the magnetic field and these transverse forces produces a distinctive long-wavelength instability at vanishing wavevector, which is absent in both non-magnetic elastic crystals and passive crystals subjected to a magnetic field. Moreover, the magnetic field provides a means of tuning the collective oscillations of the crystal, enabling the emergence of exceptional points and tuning the dynamical instability induced by odd elasticity at finite wavevectors. Our analytical results yield explicit predictions for the displacement spectrum, static structure factor, and intermediate scattering function. These findings suggest that magnetic fields could provide a powerful tool for controlling collective phenomena in high-density systems of granular or colloidal spinners.

items.title: Magnon-Phonon-Polariton Optomechanics in a van der Waals Magnet
items.summary: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2π= -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons. Our study enables direct interfacing of collective magnetic excitations with sound and light in layered van der Waals materials, paving the way for quantum-coherent transduction in the GHz range with optical readout.

items.title: Antiferromagnetic Long-Range Order in a Lattice Fermion Model
items.summary: We study a lattice fermion model with antiferromagnetic interactions on the three-dimensional cubic lattice. The hopping term of the Hamiltonian has a Weyl-type dispersion. We prove that the model has reflection positivity. Moreover, by relying on the property, we prove the existence of the antiferromagnetic long-range order at low temperatures in a strong coupling regime.

items.title: In-plane diffusion, spurious drift and a physics-structured gap predictor for a free colloidal pair
items.summary: When the diffusivity of a Brownian particle depends on position, its mean displacement acquires a noise-induced (spurious) drift whose magnitude is set by the stochastic convention $α$. Inspired by the particle-wall experiments published by G. Volpe and co-workers, we ask how much of this physics can be extracted from a pair of 1.95 $μ$m polystyrene spheres released from blinking holographic optical tweezers at five temperatures between 2 and 40 $^\circ$C. The single-sphere diffusivity inside the pair stays between 0.093 and 0.098 $μ$m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, whereas the Stokes-Einstein value for water rises from 0.126 to 0.361 $μ$m$^2$ s$^{-1}$; an isolated sphere shows the same deficit, so the missing diffusivity scale originates in the measurement and not in the pair interaction. The pair is what makes the diffusivity depend on position: from the measured gap-dependent diffusivities $D_\parallel(h)$ and $D_\perp(h)$ we build a Fokker-Planck predictor of the future gap and score it on held-out releases. It recovers the 90% width of the gap distribution up to 800 ms but cannot discriminate between $α= 0$, $1/2$ and $1$, because the $α$-dependent mean shift is an order of magnitude smaller than that width. The ensemble spurious drift is consistent with zero at both ends of the temperature range, and the regression for $α$ never exceeds $R^2 = 0.22$. We present a planar methods baseline and identify the measurements required to resolve $α$.

items.title: Shortest-path percolation and structural robustness of quantum internet networks
items.summary: We study shortest-path percolation on spatial networks that model the quantum internet based on optical fibers. In this process, the removal of paths describes the consumption of the entangled links used for communication. We compare finite and unrestricted path-length bounds for networks whose average degree either increases with system size or remains approximately constant. We show that networks become more robust as the average degree increases, whereas networks with approximately constant average degree exhibit a data collapse for the fixed finite bounds considered. Using Monte Carlo sampling of the shortest-path-length distribution, we estimate an equivalent path cost, a finite bound that approximately reproduces the degradation of the network in the unrestricted case. For networks with fixed average degree, this cost grows approximately as the square root of the number of nodes. Increasing the bound beyond this value requires additional computation time without appreciably changing the percolation dynamics. As a complementary result, for Erdős-Rényi random networks, we find an empirical relation between the initial average degree and the approximately common crossing point of the percolation curves for different path-length bounds.

items.title: High-resolution top-down nanopatterning of NbN thin films for superconducting metamaterials
items.summary: Periodic nanopatterning offers a route to tailoring vortex motion and the electromagnetic response of superconducting films, providing a basis for superconducting metamaterials. Here, we report a high-resolution top-down nanopatterning process for ultrathin epitaxial NbN films on sapphire substrates. Electron-beam lithography using hydrogen silsesquioxane (HSQ) and ZEP 530A resists was optimized through proximity-effect correction and adhesion-layer integration. Dense superconducting nanowire grids with pitches down to 70 nm were fabricated, alongside millimeter-square areas patterned with 100-nm-pitch hole arrays with high pattern fidelity. A thin Si capping layer was found to significantly improve HSQ adhesion on epitaxial NbN. The nanopatterns were successfully transferred into 5-nm-thick NbN films by reactive ion etching (RIE). Structural and dimensional characterization was performed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and atomic force microscopy (AFM), enabling cross-validation of nanoscale feature dimensions and etch quality. Electrical transport measurements reveal periodic resistance minima and switching-current oscillations at magnetic fields set by the hole-array pitch, consistent with enhanced vortex pinning when the vortex configuration matches the patterned lattice. Cryogenic THz time-domain spectroscopy further reveals a reduced superfluid density in the nanopatterned region relative to pristine NbN, while both regions have a spectroscopic superconducting transition near 14 K. These results establish a robust fabrication platform for superconducting nanopatterns targeting vortex pinning, metamaterials, and quantum-device applications.

items.title: Simple Models of Thermal Order in $2+1$ Dimensions
items.summary: Heating need not destroy order. We show that it persists to arbitrarily high temperatures in simple quantum field theories in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions. In a $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ model of two real scalar fields, a sufficiently negative mixed quartic coupling drives one field to condense, spontaneously breaking its $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry. When coupled to massless Dirac fermions through a Yukawa interaction, this condensate generates a fermion mass, thereby spontaneously breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries. We extend this construction to a $\mathbb Z_2\times O(n)$ scalar model, in which the Mermin-Wagner theorem precludes spontaneous breaking of the continuous $O(n)$ symmetry at finite temperatures. Nevertheless, for $n=2$, a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless superfluid phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures. In this phase, spatial correlations decay algebraically, with an exponent that approaches zero as the temperature increases. For $n\geq 3$, we uncover a further unexpected feature of these models: the characteristic size of ordered domains grows asymptotically with temperature, revealing an unusual enhancement of spatial correlations upon heating. We establish our results using a controlled high-temperature expansion, with selected findings corroborated by numerical functional renormalization group analysis. The simplicity of the field content in these models provides a promising starting point for exploring experimental realizations of persistent thermal order in thin-film materials.

items.title: Hidden Rotational Dynamics from Crystal Geometry
items.summary: From hidden spin order to electronic loop currents and frustrated fluctuations, unconventional quantum matter reveals the rich patterns that electronic and magnetic degrees of freedom form across space and time. Recent advances in chiral phononics have extended this perspective to lattice vibrations, raising the question of whether the lattice itself can generate spatially organized rotational correlations. Here we show that crystal geometry provides an autonomous mechanism for generating equilibrium angular-momentum circulation and staggered antisymmetric displacement interactions, independently of coupling to electronic or magnetic order. Our framework applies broadly to crystalline systems hosting locally symmetry-lowered environments embedded within a higher-symmetry global structure. We identify how directional elastic forces organize displacement correlations and how eliminating internal coordinates generates staggered antisymmetric interactions-a phononic analogue of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange-even in globally centrosymmetric crystals. By separating intersite angular-momentum transfer from crystalline restoring torques, we show that both elastic anisotropy and the induced antisymmetric interactions together drive oppositely circulating angular-momentum currents on neighboring plaquettes, despite vanishing mean angular momentum at every site. Sustained by quantum and thermal fluctuations, this circulation preserves time-reversal and inversion symmetry and requires neither external driving nor spontaneous symmetry breaking. Our results establish lattice geometry as a microscopic source of spatially organized angular-momentum dynamics.

items.title: Infrared fluctuations and collective entanglement modes in harmonic lattices
items.summary: We investigate how infrared fluctuations and spatial separation shape vacuum entanglement between two finite regions in the relativistic harmonic chain and its Lifshitz generalizations. At fixed lattice spacing and finite geometry, we establish that logarithmic negativity remains uniformly bounded as the mass approaches zero, while mutual information diverges. Infrared-enhanced total correlations therefore do not provide an unbounded distillable-entanglement resource. Using local symplectic consolidation, we identify the collective canonical modes carrying the negativity and follow their evolution with separation. Their participation crosses over from localization near the facing boundaries to a collective distribution within each region. Expansion in the adjacent-state canonical basis connects this evolution to progressively weaker, more extended reference modes, including adjacent-halo directions. Building on the established concentration of long-distance logarithmic negativity into a single canonical pair, we show that its spatial participation is smooth and infrared-dominated despite its ultraviolet canonical structure, a distinction also present in pure-state entanglement modes. These results refine the ultraviolet mode picture by resolving the long-wavelength organization of the oscillators participating in the surviving entanglement. Across the massless dispersions studied, the normalized participation approaches a universal long-distance profile when separation is scaled by the negativity radius. Its detailed form and the entanglement range nevertheless remain sensitive to ultraviolet deformations. Together, these findings distinguish infrared-enhanced correlations from distillable entanglement and reveal the collective spatial organization underlying its persistence at large separation.

items.title: A Closer Look on the Influence of Constraints Upon the Optimization of the Nonadditive Entropic Functional $S_{q}$
items.summary: The canonical distribution is obtained by maximizing the Boltzmann-Gibbs-von Neumann-Shannon entropy $S_{BG}(p)=k\sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}\ln 1/p_{i}$ constrained to $\sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}=1$ and $\sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}\,e_{i}=U$, $e_{1}\leq\ldots\leq e_{W}$ being the energies of the $W$ possible states and $U\in[e_{1},e_{W}]$ their mean value. We revisit a generalized version of this optimization problem grounded in the nonadditive entropy $S_{q}(p)=k\,(\sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}^{q}-1)/(1-q)$ (frequently, though not necessarily, $q\in(0,1)$; $S_1=S_{BG}$), and the constraint $\sum^{W}_{i=1} p_{i}^{q^{\prime}}e_{i} / \sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}^{q^{\prime}}=U$, $q^{\prime}>0$. Sufficient conditions for existence, strict positivity, and uniqueness of solutions are derived, along with a theorem that enables their closed-form calculation. We apply these results to deepen the understanding of the two standard cases in the literature ($q^{\prime}=1$ and $q^{\prime}=q$), as well as of a new one ($q^{\prime}=2-q$). We prove that these standard cases are the only ones yielding optimizing probability distributions of $q$-exponential form. Furthermore, we define an effective temperature $T_{q,q^{\prime}}$ through a Clausius-like relation $1/T_{q,q^{\prime}}=\partial S_{q} / \partial U$ and derive a Helmholtz-like energy $F_{q,q^{\prime}}=U-T_{q,q^{\prime}}S_{q}$, with the former grounding the validity of the $0^{\textrm{th}}$ Principle of Thermodynamics within this generalized statistical mechanics. Finally, we show that the case with a linear constraint (i.e., $q^{\prime}=1$) with $q\in(0,1)$ (i) preserves the Third Law of Thermodynamics; (ii) can be used to model classical many-body Hamiltonian systems with arbitrarily-ranged interactions; and (iii) resembles features of low-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems at the edge of chaos.

items.title: Scalable spin-nematic squeezing in multi-level dipole-interacting Rydberg atom arrays
items.summary: We study the dynamical generation of metrologically useful entanglement in arrays of three-level (spin-1) systems coupled by spin-exchange interactions, as realized by dipole-interacting Rydberg atoms in optical tweezers. We quantify the metrological gain by a generalized squeezing parameter optimized over all linear $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ phase generators and readout observables. For equal exchange couplings on the two transitions, the dynamics reduces to one-axis twisting (OAT) of an effective two-level system. Away from this point, the full three-level structure provides a genuine advantage. For all-to-all couplings, the optimal squeezing at $N=4000$ exceeds the OAT value by a factor of 3.6, with a fitted scaling exponent of $0.93$ compared with $0.69$ for OAT over $100\le N\le4000$. For two-dimensional dipolar arrays, exact and tensor-network simulations up to $N=49$ show that the optimal three-level protocol outperforms the effective spin-1/2 dynamics, with a gain that increases with system size, and semiclassical simulations show that squeezing continues to grow up to $N=10^4$. Crucially, our results demonstrate a real advantage of utilizing the full three-level $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ structure of the spin-1 system over $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ type one-axis twisting dynamics. Our results extend interaction-driven scalable squeezing beyond the well-studied qubit setting to spin-exchange-coupled qudits with dipolar interactions, and can be realized in current Rydberg tweezer experiments.

items.title: Symmetry-reduced k-point sampling and Wannier analysis with localized Gaussian orbitals
items.summary: Brillouin-zone sampling with localized orbitals requires consistent transformations between sparse real-space matrices and complex Bloch states. Symmetry reduces the number of reciprocal-space problems, but scalar integration weights alone cannot reconstruct the matrices and wavefunctions needed for densities and orbital analysis. We develop a unified formulation of these transformations for nonorthogonal Gaussian bases and describe its implementation in CP2K. Atom permutations, local orbital rotations, and lattice phases connect irreducible-point solutions to full symmetry orbits while preserving the overlap metric. Direct and fast lattice transforms couple this construction to self-consistent calculations, including complex orbital optimization and finite-temperature occupations. Gauge-consistent full-mesh orbitals and directed inter-point overlaps support Wannier90 export, Wannier construction, and Hamiltonian interpolation. In silicon and aluminium tests, symmetry reduces a 64-point mesh to four representatives while retaining cell energies or electronic free energies within $1.5\times10^{-12}$ hartree of the unreduced calculation. Hybrid exchange and many-body applications illustrate the additional role of auxiliary bases and transfer momenta. The resulting framework connects symmetry-reduced integration to gauge-consistent analysis of periodic electronic states within a localized-orbital representation.

items.title: Generalized Boltzmann-Gibbs Distributions and the Electronic Partition Function Paradox
items.summary: The maximization of the nonadditive entropic functional $S_{q}(p)=k\sum_{i}p_{i}\ln_{q}(1/p_{i})$, $q\in(0,1)$, under a linear mean-energy constraint, i.e., the best-behaved case from Dognini and Tsallis (2026), is used to derive generalizations of the Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution for physical systems whose description requires a limiting process over the energy spectrum: the hydrogen atom in free space; an energy spectrum that uniformly approaches a continuous, unbounded limit with a common degeneracy; the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of velocities; the harmonic oscillator; and the one-dimensional box. For the hydrogen atom with mean energy $U\in[0,e_{ion}]$, the limiting optimal distribution is a two-tier one, concentrated on the ground level and on the ionization threshold, with weights $1-U/e_{ion}$ and $U/e_{ion}$ for every $q\in(0,1)$, and the temperature rescaled by $\ln_{q}W$ is finite and given by $T_{q,s}=T_{ion}(U/e_{ion})^{1-q}$, with $T_{ion}=e_{ion}/kq$. This circumvents the Electronic Partition Function Paradox and yields a family of well-defined thermodynamic behaviors.

items.title: Hidden convexity of the Eliashberg condensation energy: existence, uniqueness and continuity of the superconducting state
items.summary: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. We establish the nonlinear part of this picture. In the variables $ρ_n=\sin^2θ_n$, the condensation energy restricted to the first quadrant is strictly convex, and folding any admissible chain into that quadrant cannot increase its energy. For every positive, non-increasing interaction with power-law decay, hidden convexity and a compactness estimate give existence and uniqueness of the minimizer up to gauge. The normal state minimizes the energy exactly when its quadratic form is non-negative, including marginal stability. Among admissible chains, a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations exists exactly when the normal state is linearly unstable and is then unique. For temperature-dependent families with pointwise continuity and locally uniform decay bounds, the minimizing density is continuous in a weighted $\ell^1$ norm. Together with uniqueness of the linear-stability temperature, these results prove the thermodynamic conjectures for the $γ$-model, Einstein phonons and general phonon spectra; the phonon applications use separately established spectral input. Finite-dimensional algebraic and convex-analytic components are machine-checked in Lean. The proofs were obtained independently of concurrent work that reaches overlapping conclusions.

items.title: Robust Passive Quantum Memory in Three Dimensions, Part I: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability
items.summary: Whether a three-dimensional quantum many-body system with geometrically local, bounded-degree interactions can passively protect encoded quantum information has remained a central open question since Kitaev introduced topological quantum computation. Passive protection requires stability against both thermal noise at nonzero temperature and generic static Hamiltonian perturbations Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin (BDL) recently established unperturbed three-dimensional thermal self-correction using a recursively defined family of stabilizer Hamiltonians. However, they left open whether their construction remains stable against quantum perturbations, even at zero temperature. In this paper, we show that a slight variant of the BDL code family achieves stability along both boundary axes of the perturbation-temperature phase diagram as the system size grows. Following BDL, in the absence of perturbation it is thermally stable below a critical temperature, achieving a stretched-exponentially long memory lifetime when coupled to any local Markovian thermal bath generated by single-site system-bath interactions satisfying detailed balance with bounded coupling rates. At zero temperature under arbitrary weak, superpolynomially decaying quantum perturbations, the family maintains a uniform bulk spectral gap, superpolynomially small ground-space splitting, and a superpolynomially long closed-system unitary memory lifetime for quasi-locally dressed logical observables. To prove this zero-temperature stability, we establish local topological quantum order across the multiscale hierarchy using a linearly dilated relaxation of the usual Bravyi-Hastings-Michalakis criteria. In the companion paper, we combine the tools developed here with finite-temperature worldline cluster expansions to establish passive self-correction throughout the phase diagram's positive-temperature perturbed interior.

items.title: Tunable Topological Charge Order in Magnetic Moiré Systems
items.summary: Two-dimensional electrons in a strong magnetic field exhibit two seemingly incompatible ground states: incompressible quantum Hall liquids with a quantized Hall conductance, and electron crystals in which interactions drive the charge into ordered patterns. Moiré superlattices in transition-metal-dichalcogenide bilayers offer a tunable arena for this competition. Using neural quantum states (NQS) together with several methodological advances, we show how this competition unfolds. In particular, we demonstrate that the two end points are separated by an extended regime in which molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. We map the ground-state phase diagram of electrons at Landau-level filling $ν_B=1$ in the presence of a moiré superlattice potential, with three electrons per moiré cell. In the deep triangular potential limit, the electrons form the topologically trivial "Wigner molecular crystal'' of three-electron artificial atoms, a state recently imaged at zero magnetic field in moiré bilayers. As the potential depth is lowered, molecular charge order remains while quantized Hall response emerges. At the honeycomb point, where each cell contains three electrons and two degenerate moiré minima, wells are either singly or doubly occupied and the doublons provide an emergent Ising degree of freedom. Starting from modest interaction strength, we find short-range doublon correlations within the Chern insulator which grow with interaction strength and eventually break sublattice symmetry, forming a Néel CDW with long-range order between doublons. The topological molecular regime lies at twist angles and magnetic fields directly accessible to current experiments. The methodological advances presented provide a scalable framework for exploring a broad range of questions in correlated quantum matter in the presence of magnetic fields.

items.title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
items.summary: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $θ=π$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.

items.title: Parametric and Universal Thouless Invariants in Matrix Product States
items.summary: We investigate the classification of continuous families of translation-invariant injective matrix product states on an infinite chain, parametrized by a paracompact Hausdorff space $X$ and subject to a compact Hausdorff symmetry $G$. We construct an invariant for phases of such families, valued in $\check{H}^1(X;\widehat{G})$, that generalizes the known $\widehat{G}$ phase invariant for $G$-symmetric Thouless pumps. The phase invariant is constructed as the pullback to $X$ of a single universal Čech cohomology class on a classifying space of $G$-symmetric translation-invariant injective matrix product states. Several examples are given over various parameter spaces where this invariant is nontrivial.

items.title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
items.summary: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.

items.title: Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
items.summary: A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $ρ$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $ρ$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $ρ-1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.

items.title: The SymTFT and Quantum Phases of Matter
items.summary: The symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) provides a unified framework for ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems. By encoding symmetry in a topological theory in one higher dimension, it separates symmetry data from the details of a specific quantum system. In this review, we give a pedagogical introduction to this framework and survey its applications to phases of quantum matter. For fusion category symmetries in ${(1+1)}$d, we explain how the SymTFT characterizes anomalies, classifies gapped phases, and organizes the symmetry structure of gapless phases. We also give a broad overview of further developments of this framework, including extensions to symmetries in higher dimensions, continuous symmetries, fermionic systems, mixed states, and spacetime symmetries.

items.title: Hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in the iron garnet Almandine Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$
items.summary: Antiferromagnets on the hyperkagome lattice provide a three-dimensional route to strong magnetic frustration, but experimentally accessible realizations with well-established microscopic Hamiltonians remain scarce. Garnets are a broad family of materials in which magnetic ions can form two interpenetrating hyperkagome lattices, giving rise to spin glass, spin-liquid and hidden-order physics. Here we identify the iron aluminosilicate garnet almandine, Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$, as a spin-$2$ hyperkagome antiferromagnet. Using density functional theory energy mapping, we determine a Heisenberg Hamiltonian for the high-spin Fe$^{2+}$ moments and find dominant nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, as well as significant longer-range interactions. Classical Monte Carlo simulations of this Hamiltonian, combined with quantum-to-classical rescaling of the spin length, show a transition to antiferromagnetic order at $T_{\rm N}\approx9.8$K, in excellent agreement with specific heat experiments. The resulting non-collinear magnetic state is naturally described by magnetic toroidal octupolar order, which we connect to known results for the highly frustrated hyperkagome antiferromagnet gadolinium gallium garnet, Gd$_3$Ga$_5$O$_{12}$. We also calculate magnetic neutron diffraction amplitudes as well as static and dynamic structure factors using semiclassical dynamics, providing quantitative predictions for future neutron scattering experiments. Our results establish almandine as a chemically accessible realization of frustrated hyperkagome magnetism in the garnet family.

items.title: Double quantum dots as dynamical impurities in one-dimensional transport
items.summary: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. For a single impurity, we solve the scattering problem exactly and show Feshbach-like perfect elastic reflection, whose resonant condition distinguishes the initial two-level state. For several impurities in a strongly reflecting chain, transmission peaks at an intermediate mean level splitting. At small splittings, energy exchange with the impurities can weaken constructive interference between backscattered paths, consistent with the initial rise in transmission. As excitation channels close, virtual transitions can enhance reflection and drive transmission below its purely elastic value $T_0$. At larger splittings, these virtual processes weaken and transmission approaches $T_0$. We discuss how gate-controlled transmission measurements in quantum-dot arrays could test these predictions.

items.title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
items.summary: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

items.title: Emission and Absorption of Microwave Photons in Orthogonal Temporal Modes across a 30-Meter Two-Node Network
items.summary: The tunable interaction between stationary quantum bits and propagating modes of light allows for the encoding of quantum information in the state of itinerant photons. items.summary: Non-Abelian gauge fields provide a powerful framework for exploring exotic topological states, yet their interplay with space-time symmetries remains largely unexplored. Cao et al. introduce the concept of non-Abelian space-time lattice gauge fields and experimentally realize them using space-time topolectrical circuits, revealing geometry-dependent higher-order topological states and unconventional topological phase transitions with indirect band crossings. This opens avenues for exploring non-Abelian topological physics beyond the limitations of static systems.

Stavropoulou et al. simultaneously track molecular relaxation and densification during physical aging of a molecular glass and show that the two evolve in strict proportionality. The proportionality factor is predicted, without adjustable parameters, from equilibrium density scaling parameters, extending this framework to the nonequilibrium glassy state.

We further show that if we allow for non-local gates, the Gibbs state of the periodic 1D Ising model can be prepared in logarithmic depth and linearly many simultaneous measurements.

items.title: An active Lorentz gas: walking droplets in periodic media
authors: Aleksi Majaniemi, Esko Toivonen, Rahil N Valani, Rainer Klages and Esa Räsänen
items.summary: The Lorentz gas is a paradigmatic model in dynamical systems theory for understanding the origin of nonequilibrium transport in terms of microscopic deterministic chaos. In the periodic setting, a point particle scatters elastically off disks arranged on a two-dimensional lattice. Here we replace the disks by smooth potentials and the particle by the widely studied walking droplet, which propels itself on a vertically vibrating fluid. In the low-memory limit, this droplet reduces to a particle with nonlinear active friction. We call this system an active Lorentz gas. Using extensive numerical simulations, we analyse how dissipation generated by the active deterministic dynamics alters the phase-space structure of the corresponding conservative Lorentz gas. We find that islands of stability collapse into attracting and repelling sets. To characterize these structures, we introduce an energy-variance filtering method that distinguishes localized periodic, quasi-ballistic periodic, and chaotic trajectories, enabling the construction of bifurcation diagrams in a non-conservative setting. We identify parameter regimes exhibiting strong bifurcation cascades, anomalous diffusion, and significant phase-space contraction. Our results establish the active Lorentz gas as a rich framework for studying transport in dissipative dynamical systems and provide a bridge between active matter and classical models of chaotic transport, with potential implications for hydrodynamic quantum analogs in periodic media.

items.title: Three-dimensional topological disclination in acoustic crystals
authors: Zhenxiao Zhu, Yan Meng, Minmiao Wang, Xiang Xi, Yuxin Zhong, Linyun Yang, Bei Yan, Jingming Chen, Ziyao Wang, Thomas Christensen, Caigui Jiang, Changqing Xu, Ce Shang, Zhen Gao
items.summary: Topological disclinations are rotational-symmetry-breaking lattice defects that can probe crystalline topology and offer a versatile platform for topological cavities, waveguides, and lasers. Here, Zhu et al. report a three-dimensional topological disclination that carries a fractional charge of 1/2 and hosts zero-dimensional topological bound states embedded in the bulk. The result extends disclination physics beyond layered or surface-based designs and opens new possibilities for controlling waves through the interplay of band topology and defect geometry in three dimensions.

items.title: Coupled propagation of acoustic topological states
authors: Ming-Zhu Li, Lei Shi, Zhe-Yu Ji, Zhaojiang Chen and Ya-Xi Shen
items.summary: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupled propagation of two pseudospin states in an acoustic topological heterostructure. Within the framework of coupled-mode theory, the heterostructure is mapped onto a two-waveguide model, in which the two pseudospin topological states serve as guiding modes. The propagation constants of the individual topological states and the coupling strength between them are quantitatively extracted from the projected band structures of supercells. When the two topological states are decoupled, acoustic energy remains confined to the excited topological interface. When the two topological states are coupled, acoustic energy undergoes Bloch oscillation between two topological interfaces. Notably, the energy-transfer coefficient of the Bloch oscillation can be tuned by introducing interface detuning. Owing to the frequency dispersion of the coupling strength, the heterostructure can function as a wavelength-selective demultiplexer. This work establishes a generalized coupled-mode framework for the quantitative analysis and flexible manipulation of topological-state coupling, offering new insights into the design of topologically protected acoustic devices with controllable multichannel functionalities.

items.title: Toward Unified and Accurate Description of Multidimensional Nuclear Observables via a Prior-Informed Large Language Model
authors: Shijie Guo, 世杰 郭, Shouyu Wang, 守宇 王, Enhong Wang, 恩宏 王, Zhongming Niu, 中明 牛, Yiming Ding and 一鸣 丁
items.summary: A prior-informed large language model (LLM)-driven multi-task learning framework is proposed for the unified and accurate description of multiple nuclear observables. By fine-tuning the pre-trained DeepSeek-R1-1.5B model with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), lightweight adapters are introduced while preserving general pre-trained parameters. Under a causal language modeling paradigm, the model is trained autoregressively on deviations between experimental and theoretical values. Significant accuracy improvements are achieved across seven observables, including charge radii, masses, binding energies, separation energies, and decay energies, with the training loss decreasing by over 98% across all tasks. This demonstrates that the LLM-based framework, through structured prior embedding, offers an efficient and shared approach for multi-task regression in fundamental nuclear properties.

items.title: On the Precise Boundary of the Néel Antiferromagnetic Phase in the Shastry-Sutherland Model
authors: Rongyi Lv, 融一 吕, Xiangjian Qian, 湘坚 钱, Mingpu Qin and 明普 秦
items.summary: The ground state phase diagram of the Shastry-Sutherland model remains controversial. In particular, the nature of the transition between the plaquette valence bond solid (PVBS) phase and the Néel antiferromagnetic (AFM) phase is still under debate. While some studies suggest a direct transition between the two phases, others propose the existence of a narrow intermediate quantum spin liquid regime. To address this issue, we perform large-scale Density Matrix Renormalization Group calculations to determine the Néel AFM phase boundary in the Shastry-Sutherland model. By applying staggered boundary pinning fields and directly measuring the bulk staggered magnetization, and through systematic extrapolations with respect to truncation error as well as careful finite-size scaling, we find that the staggered magnetization remains finite across the controversial region 0.78 ≲J1/J2 ≤ 0.81, which was suggested to host a quantum spin liquid phase in some studies. Together with the previously established consensus placing the PVBS phase boundary at J1/J2 ≈ 0.78, these results, within the resolution of the present calculations, provide evidence against the existence of an intermediate quantum spin liquid phase and support a direct PVBS–Néel AFM transition in the Shastry-Sutherland model.

items.title: 2D quantum-path interference in high-harmonic generation driven by highly-bichromatic fields
authors: Xiaozhou Zou, Lucie Jurkovičová, Anne Weber, Cong Zhao, Martin Albrecht, Ondřej Finke, Alexandr Vendl, Annika Grenfell, Wojciech Szuba, Jaroslav Nejdl, Eric Constant, Margarita Khokhlova, Emilio Pisanty, Ondřej Hort and Amelle Zaïr
items.summary: We experimentally observe a new type of quantum-path interference, in two-dimensions (2D-QPI), in high-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by an orthogonally-polarised highly-bichromatic field. This regime is characterised by a relatively strong orthogonal second-harmonic component beyond the weak perturbation limit, such that the electron dynamics are substantially modified. In this highly-bichromatic regime, we demonstrate that 2D-QPI is encoded in the measured harmonic intensity modulations with respect to the relative phase of the two-colour field. The modulations of the odd-order harmonics show a monomodal behaviour, whereas the even harmonics are modulated in a bimodal structure. Our calculations using the strong-field approximation and saddle-point method disentangle contributions from multiple quantum orbits in this HHG regime, revealing that the dipole response for both odd and even harmonics inherits the dynamic symmetry of the orthogonally-polarised driving field. This new type of 2D-QPI offers a novel route to HHG spectroscopy of attosecond electron dynamics by lifting up the dimensionality of the quantum paths involved in the interference.
